## 20260515T004946Z-slumbot-torch-levelsync-cuda-integration - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T00:49:46Z
- Type: protected integration diagnostic
- Gate: TDD + methodology-review + objective-audit + live smoke
- Hypothesis: The new level-synchronous Torch CUDA resolver should be callable
  from live Slumbot smoke paths explicitly, without changing the default solver
  backend or promotion policy.
- Failure class: compute_integration
- Summary: Extended Slumbot and autoresearch CLI backend choices to accept
  `torch-levelsync-cuda` and `torch-levelsync-cpu`, while leaving `auto` on the
  stable CPU path. Added regression tests for queue forwarding and Slumbot help
  exposure.
- Evidence:
  - Review: `autoresearch-session/poker_reviews/20260515T004500Z-torch-levelsync-cuda-cfr`
  - Tests: `uv run pytest -q test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch.py test/unit/test_slumbot_diagnostics.py test/unit/test_solver_backend.py` -> `67 passed`.
  - Objective audit with review passed for `scripts/play_slumbot.py`,
    `scripts/poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py`, `scripts/poker_autoresearch.py`,
    and the new tests.
  - Live smoke: `uv run python scripts/poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py --model models/slumbot_2p_iter1000.pt --hands 3 --greedy --no-allin --solver-backend torch-levelsync-cuda --timeout-seconds 600` -> passed.
- Metrics: live smoke had `0` API errors, `0` parse errors, `2` solver
  decisions, mean reported solver latency `1270.3 ms`, max `1593.3 ms`, mean
  solver hands `1005.5`, and elapsed `2.031 s/hand`.
- Decision: integration is valid but not promoted. Do not flip `auto` to CUDA
  until mixed turn/river fixed-state parity and live latency attribution show
  that the end-to-end path beats CPU on the same states.

## 20260515T005447Z-resolver-latency-attribution-metrics - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T00:54:47Z
- Type: protected evaluation diagnostic
- Gate: TDD + methodology-review + related-work check + objective-audit
- Hypothesis: Separating inner CFR recurrence latency from resolver setup
  overhead will explain why the CUDA level-sync recurrence does not fully
  translate into live Slumbot latency.
- Failure class: compute_integration
- Related work: GPU-CFR supports coarse matrix/vector boundaries for GPU
  acceleration; DeepStack supports end-to-end continual resolving latency as
  the relevant online boundary. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14778,
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.01724, and
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28254783/.
- Summary: Added per-case and aggregate latency attribution to the fixed
  resolver benchmark: total solver path, `StreetSolver.solve(...)` CFR
  recurrence time, and residual setup overhead.
- Evidence:
  - Review: `autoresearch-session/poker_reviews/20260515T005447Z-resolver-latency-attribution-metrics`
  - Manifest: `docs/research_protocols/poker_review_manifests/20260515T005447Z-resolver-latency-attribution-metrics.json`
  - CPU artifact: `autoresearch-session/search_consistency_restored200_100x2k_20260513/resolver_benchmark_cpu_iter10_mixed4_attribution_seed20260515.json`
  - CUDA artifact: `autoresearch-session/search_consistency_restored200_100x2k_20260513/resolver_benchmark_torch_levelsync_cuda_iter10_mixed4_attribution_seed20260515.json`
  - Focused test: `uv run pytest -q test/unit/test_resolver_benchmark.py::test_resolver_benchmark_reports_fixed_state_policy_and_solver_metrics` -> `1 passed`.
- Metrics: fixed mixed four-state CFR10 CPU averaged `568.4 ms` total,
  `325.4 ms` CFR, and `243.1 ms` overhead. `torch-levelsync-cuda` averaged
  `329.2 ms` total, `94.0 ms` CFR, and `235.2 ms` overhead.
- Decision: keep the metric as diagnostic instrumentation. The next compute
  target is setup overhead, especially turn equity/payoff matrix and tree
  construction, not another recurrence-only CUDA port.

## 20260515T010338Z-incremental-turn-equity-evaluator - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T01:03:38Z
- Type: protected solver performance change
- Gate: TDD + methodology-review + related-work check + objective-audit +
  solver/regression tests + live smoke
- Hypothesis: Precomputing six-card base ranks during turn equity construction
  should avoid redundant five-card subset evaluations and reduce setup
  overhead without changing solver semantics.
- Failure class: compute_integration
- Related work: Cactus Kev-style prime-product lookup evaluators support fast
  five-card rank lookup; this change reuses that local evaluator while avoiding
  redundant best-five-of-seven subset work. Sources:
  https://suffe.cool/poker/evaluator.html and
  https://pokerkit.readthedocs.io/en/0.6/evaluation.html.
- Summary: Added `_evaluate_six_eval_cards` and
  `_evaluate_seven_eval_cards_with_six_base`, then used the incremental path
  inside turn equity matrix construction. Also added direct tests that compare
  the incremental evaluator against the existing full seven-card evaluator.
- Evidence:
  - Review: `autoresearch-session/poker_reviews/20260515T010338Z-incremental-turn-equity-evaluator`
  - Manifest: `docs/research_protocols/poker_review_manifests/20260515T010338Z-incremental-turn-equity-evaluator.json`
  - CPU artifact: `autoresearch-session/search_consistency_restored200_100x2k_20260513/resolver_benchmark_cpu_iter10_mixed4_incremental_eval_seed20260515.json`
  - CUDA artifact: `autoresearch-session/search_consistency_restored200_100x2k_20260513/resolver_benchmark_torch_levelsync_cuda_iter10_mixed4_incremental_eval_seed20260515.json`
  - Tests: `uv run pytest -q test/unit/test_solver_backend.py test/unit/test_resolver_benchmark.py test/unit/test_cfr_budget_frontier.py test/unit/test_solver_update_gate.py` -> `52 passed`.
  - Live smoke: `uv run python scripts/poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py --model models/slumbot_2p_iter1000.pt --hands 3 --greedy --no-allin --solver-backend torch-levelsync-cuda --timeout-seconds 600` -> passed.
- Metrics: fixed mixed four-state CFR10 `torch-levelsync-cuda` improved from
  `329.2 ms` total, `94.0 ms` CFR, `235.2 ms` overhead to `298.4 ms` total,
  `93.2 ms` CFR, `205.2 ms` overhead. CPU improved from `568.4/325.4/243.1 ms`
  to `541.6/326.1/215.5 ms`.
- Decision: keep the optimization. It is a real setup win but not sufficient
  for CUDA auto-promotion; next work should isolate live-only setup costs such
  as range pruning, tree construction, and CPU-to-GPU tensor preparation.

  `924 ms`, but online decision latency was `1571 ms` (`1.7670x` live). Split B

  state features, blueprint/search entropy, margins, or early trace signals,
  then rerun the same root-disjoint gate.

## 2026-05-10 Minimum Raise Parity Fix

- Timestamp: 2026-05-10T18:23:21Z
- Type: audit_fix
- Failure class: action_mapping
- Summary: Slumbot diagnostics showed live action-mapping drift for under-minimum fractional raises. CPU full-deck, fast-state, CUDA, Slumbot play, and range-tracker legal masks now require each fractional raise bucket to meet the no-limit minimum raise contribution before it is legal.
- Verification: `pytest -q test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_eval.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py test/unit/test_slumbot_diagnostics.py test/unit/test_network_mask.py test/unit/test_slumbot_mapping.py test/unit/test_legal_mask_parity.py`; `/usr/bin/env NUMBA_ENABLE_CUDASIM=1 python scripts/test_feature_encoding.py`; direct CUDA-sim legal-mask probe.

## 2026-05-10 GPU Training Readiness Fix

- Timestamp: 2026-05-10T18:36:07Z
- Type: audit_fix
- Failure class: compute_bottleneck
- Summary: Numba CUDA compilation failed because NVVM was not discoverable from the active Python env. Installed `nvidia-cuda-nvcc-cu12==12.6.85`, added the missing `libnvvm.so.4` compatibility symlink, and added `scripts/cuda_env.py` so GPU scripts set `CUDA_HOME` plus `NUMBA_FORCE_CUDA_CC=8.6` inside Python before importing Numba.
- Verification: `pytest -q test/unit/test_cuda_env.py test/unit/test_train_slumbot_args.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_eval.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py test/unit/test_slumbot_diagnostics.py test/unit/test_network_mask.py test/unit/test_slumbot_mapping.py test/unit/test_legal_mask_parity.py`; one-iteration Slumbot GPU training smoke saved `models/autoresearch_minraise_smoke/corrected_minraise_final.pt` with `device=cuda`, `traverse=2.3s`, `train=0.6s`.

## 2026-05-10 GPU Replay Cache OOM Fix

- Timestamp: 2026-05-10T18:42:00Z
- Type: audit_fix
- Failure class: compute_bottleneck
- Summary: The 300-iteration corrected-minimum-raise training gate failed at iteration 13 with CUDA OOM after the 10M replay buffer pushed GPU cache usage near the 8GB card limit. Added a memory-budget guard so `_MultiBufferView` skips the GPU replay cache when its estimated tensor footprint would consume too much free GPU memory.
- Verification: `pytest -q test/unit/test_gpu_cache_budget.py test/unit/test_cuda_env.py test/unit/test_train_slumbot_args.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_eval.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py test/unit/test_slumbot_diagnostics.py test/unit/test_network_mask.py test/unit/test_slumbot_mapping.py test/unit/test_legal_mask_parity.py`.

## 20260511T140726Z-compact-gpu-replay-cache-reduces-memory-budget - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-11T14:07:26Z
- Type: audit_fix
- Failure class: compute_bottleneck
- Summary: Added compact GPU replay-cache storage for features and advantages, keeping iterations in fp32 and promoting compact advantage targets back to fp32 in the loss path. The GPU trainer now releases traversal workspace before training and releases replay cache after training so PyTorch cached memory does not starve the next Numba traversal. A reuse-budget guard keeps full-cache rebuilds off when the per-iteration training draw is much smaller than the replay buffer.
- Metrics: Compact replay-cache estimate for 20,000,000 samples is 5.104 GiB versus 10.133 GiB with float32 feature/advantage tensors. Direct CUDA probe returned `features=torch.float16`, `advantages=torch.float16`, and `iterations=torch.float32`. A 1,000,000-sample synthetic replay benchmark with 125 batches of 8,192 samples measured 0.235s host fallback versus 0.065s compact cache (`3.629x` faster). A 30-iteration Slumbot-track training benchmark crossed the 20,000,000-sample buffer mark without CUDA OOM and held steady at roughly `traverse=1.6-1.7s`, `train=1.0-1.1s`, `iter=2.8-2.9s` after warmup.
- Verification: `pytest -q test/unit/test_gpu_cache_budget.py test/unit/test_cuda_env.py test/unit/test_train_slumbot_args.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_eval.py test/unit/test_poker_autoresearch_slumbot.py test/unit/test_slumbot_diagnostics.py test/unit/test_network_mask.py test/unit/test_slumbot_mapping.py test/unit/test_legal_mask_parity.py`; `/usr/bin/env NUMBA_ENABLE_CUDASIM=1 /home/max/miniconda3/bin/python scripts/test_feature_encoding.py`; `/home/max/miniconda3/bin/python scripts/train_slumbot_2p.py --n-iterations 3 --n-traversals 100 --n-training-steps 50 --buffer-capacity 200000 --hidden-dim 128 --n-layers 2 --batch-size 512 --save-dir models/autoresearch_compact_cache_smoke_20260511T1401Z --prefix compact_cache_smoke --eval-every 0 --save-every 0`; `/home/max/miniconda3/bin/python scripts/train_slumbot_2p.py --n-iterations 30 --n-traversals 800 --n-training-steps 500 --buffer-capacity 10000000 --hidden-dim 512 --n-layers 4 --batch-size 2048 --save-dir models/autoresearch_compact_cache_benchmark_20260511T1416Z --prefix compact_cache --eval-every 0 --save-every 0`.

## 20260513T071538Z-leaf-cache-error-attribution - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-13T07:15:38Z
- Type: workflow
- Gate: manual-leaf-cache-error-attribution
- Hypothesis: Before building another learned-leaf mechanism, cached exact leaf labels should expose whether high-drift errors are broad or concentrated in specific terminal action families.
- Failure class: search_integration
- Related work: DeepStack and Supremus support depth-limited continual resolving with learned counterfactual value networks (https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.01724 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.10442), while ReBeL and Student of Games point toward public-belief-state search/value learning rather than single-state action distillation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13544 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03178). Safe/nested subgame solving also warns that imperfect-information subgames depend on the broader strategy context, so leaf replacement must be evaluated through search behavior, not only per-hand MAE (https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.02955).
- Summary: Added `scripts/analyze_dual_cfv_cache_errors.py`, which loads an existing exact dual-CFV cache, optionally merges leaf-export metadata by label, derives structural fields such as action shape and bet count, and groups model errors/residuals without re-solving. A feasibility check showed one exact river leaf label still costs about `9.0s` even with one CFR iteration, so a full exact-leaf oracle callback for the `0128` case would require thousands of solver calls and is not practical. Cache attribution shows the high-drift model is not failing uniformly: the worst MAE group is `ck/b200c/b150b525c/` at `0.1840`, while `ck/b200c/b150b712c/` has the largest residual miss at `0.1192`; simple call-through `ck/b200c/b150c/` is lowest at `0.1422` MAE and `0.0619` residual miss. On the broader 50-state rotated holdout, error increases with terminal betting complexity: bet-count `0`/`1`/`2` MAE is `0.1805`/`0.2003`/`0.2423`, while bet-count `4`/`5`/`6` is `0.3558`/`0.4175`/`0.5234`. Zero-sum projection removes predicted residual by construction but keeps the high-drift worst group near the same MAE (`0.1815`), so the next mechanism should target richer continuation values and terminal/bet-structure coverage rather than projection or uncertainty gates.

## 20260513T103441Z-successor-frontier-reach-shift - failed

Completing the full root-disjoint high-bet train pool produced `119` cuts, but the same three holdout shapes remained absent and the model still failed (`MAE/RMSE 0.3653/0.4657` vs best constant `0.3184/0.3935`). This falsifies early target truncation as the main explanation. The next principled step is not another small MLP or filter; it should build a broader successor-frontier pool/split that explicitly audits action-shape and reach coverage before training, or move to a range-conditioned residual objective.

Next work should avoid hard value substitution and test safer integration: calibrated residual values, value mixing/warm-start priors, uncertainty-aware cut selection, or direct policy/value training at the resolver action boundary.

- Type: experiment

- Hypothesis: A calibrated policy-head distribution can serve as a soft prior to improve a cheap low-iteration resolver relative to a stronger reference solver, without directly selecting the network argmax.
- Failure class: search_integration
- Summary: Added `scripts/eval_policy_prior_solver_budget.py` to compare three distributions on the same fixed cases: low-budget solver, policy-head-only, and a fixed `0.25` mixture of low-budget solver plus policy head, all measured against a `25`-iteration solver reference. On the `64` held-out policy cases, the `5`-iteration solver was already closer to the `25`-iteration reference than the soft prior mix: mean L1 `0.5778` for low solver versus `0.5950` for the mix. Mixed action agreement did not improve (`0.5469`, same as low solver), and the all-in top-action rate stayed at `0.6563`. The calibrated policy alone was farther from the reference (`0.8097` L1). This falsifies naive final-distribution mixing as a useful policy prior. A real prior must enter the CFR update/warm-start mechanism or be trained against low-vs-high solver residual behavior, not mixed after the solve.

- Failure class: transfer_gap
- Summary: Ran stochastic policy-head local smoke against random and duplicate-swapped head-to-head against the base restored checkpoint. The small random-opponent smoke was positive on average (`+166.1 chips/hand`) but had negative lower95 (`-62.1`). Next mechanism should either train all-street policy targets or evaluate a mixed path that uses regret/blueprint for unsupported early streets and the calibrated stochastic policy head only where search targets exist.

This supports action-boundary auxiliary supervision as the next diagnostic path, not gameplay promotion.

- Hypothesis: If the root-policy auxiliary failed because each exact public-state solve produced only one sampled private-hand policy target, then exporting every legal private hand's exact root strategy from the same solve should reduce all-in collapse and improve held-out root-policy distribution fit.
- Failure class: partial_distribution_transfer

The next mechanism should evaluate the learned distribution as a soft or stochastic search prior on a fresh held-out slice, not lower thresholds on this one.

## 20260513T173500Z-compute-bottleneck-not-established - note

- Timestamp: 2026-05-13T17:35:00Z
- Type: interpretation
- Gate: manual-research-log-correction
- Hypothesis: The current search-consistency failures should not be attributed to insufficient personal-PC compute until profiling demonstrates that the GPU/training pipeline is saturated and that available acceleration paths have been exhausted.
- Failure class: unproven_compute_bottleneck
- Related work: DeepStack/ReBeL show that strong poker systems can be bottlenecked by public-belief target generation and search-aligned training data, but they do not justify treating compute as the blocker before measuring utilization. Their core lesson for this project is to learn the solver-compatible object on the resolver distribution, then scale the proven path.
- Summary: The current evidence points first to target/search-interface mismatch: static successor CFV targets, dynamic cut targets, dense all-hand root-policy distillation, and naive policy warm-starts all failed held-out resolver behavior gates. Compute is not yet a demonstrated blocker. The user observed low GPU utilization, and the workflow has not yet produced a clean profiler report showing sustained GPU saturation, CPU/GPU overlap, dataloader utilization, kernel occupancy, or the effect of modern training settings such as AMP with FP16/BF16 where supported, TF32 matmul, larger batches, fused/compiled training steps, and persistent target-generation workers. Future reports must separate `algorithmic bottleneck` from `systems bottleneck`: before saying local compute is limiting, provide a short profiler-backed A/B showing where wall time goes and whether mixed precision or batching materially changes samples/sec or train sec/iter.
- Metrics file: none; this is a corrective interpretation note based on the failed search-consistency experiments above and the absence of a profiler-backed compute-saturation report.

- Type: diagnostic

- Hypothesis: The next principled step is to falsify both explanations separately: profile whether policy-head training is under-optimized, and attribute held-out policy failure to solver instability, public-root distribution, or model confidence/pathology before adding more research knobs.
- Failure class: partial_systems_underoptimization_and_policy_transfer_gap
- Related work: DeepStack/ReBeL motivate learning search-compatible public-belief objects; Deep CFR motivates average-policy distillation but does not remove the need for held-out public-state generalization. The systems lesson is separate: efficient training matters only after the search target is aligned with the gameplay interface.
- Summary: Added `scripts/profile_joint_pbs_training.py` and `scripts/analyze_joint_pbs_policy_alignment.py` with unit tests. On the exact policy-only joint-PBS artifact from the failed 25-iteration distillation run, a repeat training profile showed the FP32/no-TF32 baseline at `262008` samples/sec with only `48.0%` average sampled GPU utilization. TF32 improved to `305239` samples/sec (`1.165x`), AMP FP16 to `471340` (`1.799x`), AMP BF16 to `495340` (`1.891x`), and AMP FP16 with batch `16384` to `616427` (`2.353x`) with `96.75%` average sampled GPU utilization and `4633 MiB` peak allocated memory. The 5-vs-25 iteration exact solver comparison had top-1 `0.765625`, mean L1 `0.525374`, and model-error correlation to low/high solver disagreement only `-0.0924`, so the worst model errors are not mainly solver-budget instability. They are overconfident action/all-in transfer errors on unseen public roots.

## 20260513T183500Z-root-split-leakage-policy-transfer - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-13T18:35:00Z
- Type: diagnostic
- Gate: manual-root-split-leakage-debug
- Hypothesis: The apparent internal policy-distillation fit is inflated because the split is row-disjoint but not public-root-disjoint; all-hand policy targets create many private-hand rows per public root, so a row split validates on public roots already seen during training.
- Failure class: validation_leakage_public_root_generalization
- Related work: Public-belief search systems such as DeepStack/ReBeL require generalization over public states, not just over private hands within an already-seen public state. A split that shares public roots measures the wrong quantity for gameplay search integration.
- Summary: Audited the failed 25-iteration policy-only dataset and found that the original train/internal-holdout split had `128` train roots, `128` holdout roots, and `128` overlapping roots. It split private-hand rows inside each public root, not public roots. This explains the misleading internal score (`0.279322` L1, `0.8353` top-1): the model was tested on seen public roots. Added optional `--group-field root_label` support to `scripts/split_joint_pbs_by_metadata.py` plus a regression test enforcing root-disjoint train/holdout groups. Re-splitting the same `128`-root policy-only target set with `--group-field root_label` produced `96` train roots, `32` holdout roots, and `0` root overlap. Retraining the same `96x32` joint-PBS policy head on this corrected split dropped holdout performance to `0.847682` L1 and `0.551668` top-1, despite still beating legal-uniform L1 (`0.997732`). This identifies the main recurring misalignment cause: the old internal validation measured hand-level interpolation within seen public roots, while gameplay requires public-root extrapolation. Legal-uniform-only pass criteria are too weak for root-policy promotion.

## 20260513T190500Z-low-solver-residual-rootdisjoint - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-13T19:05:00Z
- Type: experiment
- Gate: manual-low-solver-conditioned-residual
- Hypothesis: If direct high-budget policy distillation fails because the model is trying to learn the full search distribution from public features alone, then conditioning on a cheap 5-iteration resolver policy and learning only a residual correction to the 25-iteration target should improve true public-root-disjoint holdout behavior.
- Failure class: residual_policy_transfer_gap
- Related work: ReBeL/DeepStack-style systems use search at decision time and learned networks at search-compatible interfaces; a residual-to-cheap-search target is more aligned with that interface than replacing search with a standalone cloned policy. Strategy warm-start work also suggests that learned policy information must be calibrated before it is injected into search.
- Summary: Made root-disjoint evaluation mandatory in `eval_joint_pbs_continuation_probe.py` whenever train/holdout metadata expose `root_label`, with `--allow-root-overlap` reserved for diagnostics. Added `scripts/train_joint_pbs_low_solver_residual.py`, which solves each public root once with a cheap low-iteration resolver, uses that strategy as base logits, and trains a neural delta toward the high-budget all-hand policy target. On the corrected 96-train-root / 32-holdout-root split, low-solver coverage was complete (`108288` train rows and `36096` holdout rows filled; no skipped roots). The cheap 5-iteration solver itself was much stronger than the direct root-disjoint cloned policy: holdout L1 `0.488658`, KL `0.238154`, top-1 `0.781056`. This suggests the immediate blocker is not just neural capacity; the correction target needs calibration/uncertainty structure or direct integration into search, rather than another unconstrained policy head.

ReBeL reinforces training/search on public belief states and recursive solving; PyStack shows the DeepStack-style continual resolving/value-network interface (`ContinualResolving`, `Resolving`, `Lookahead`, `NextRoundValue`); Deep CFR remains relevant for average-strategy baselines but is not the right integration surface for this failure. ## 20260513T203000Z-callback-state-dcvn-smoke - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-13T20:30:00Z
- Type: experiment
- Gate: manual-callback-state-dcvn-smoke
- Hypothesis: If the DCVN leaf failure is caused by training on root public states while search queries deeper callback leaf states with dynamic CFR reaches, then training dual-CFV values on the actual callback-state distribution should improve held-out leaf substitution behavior.
- Failure class: partial_callback_state_alignment
- Related work: DeepStack/PyStack and ReBeL both imply that learned values should be trained on the same public-belief state distribution where recursive solving queries them. This experiment tests that interface directly instead of adding another root-policy clone or capacity sweep.
- Summary: Added `scripts/build_public_belief_callback_leaf_targets.py`, which runs the CPU street solver with a non-mutating `showdown_leaf_fn`, records the exact callback states queried during CFR, converts default CFR numerator values back into per-hand EV labels using reach denominators, and saves a dual-CFV cache compatible with the existing trainer. Built a small train cache from roots `0..3` (`2048` kept callback states from `4140` seen) and a root-disjoint holdout cache from roots `128..131` (`1773` kept from `3276` seen). A tiny deepset dual-CFV checkpoint trained on these callback states beat zero/train-mean MAE but not train-mean RMSE, so the supervised checkpoint gate remained failed. However, when evaluated as a learned leaf on the same root-disjoint holdout slice, it passed the small diagnostic A/B: unprojected leaf substitution reached `0.50` action agreement and `0.3551` mean L1 drift; projected substitution reached `0.75` action agreement and `0.3977` mean L1 drift. This is the strongest evidence so far that distribution alignment, not merely model size, is the main DCVN integration issue. It is still only a 4-root smoke and is not promotable.

## 20260515T071500Z-corrected-pool-telemetry-ab - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T07:15:00Z
- Type: traversal_fidelity_ab_diagnostic
- Gate: telemetry-enabled default-vs-1000 slot comparison
- Hypothesis: Increasing per-traversal slots may create a good enough
  corrected-semantics training point without changing the algorithm.
- Failure class: traversal_fidelity_and_throughput_tradeoff
- Related work: Deep CFR uses external-sampling MCCFR and explores all actions
  at traverser infosets; MCCFR is unbiased because sampled regrets are
  corrected by the sampling scheme. Sources:
  https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/brown19b/brown19b.pdf,
  https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/3713-monte-carlo-sampling-for-regret-minimization-in-extensive-games,
  and
  https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/4569-efficient-monte-carlo-counterfactual-regret-minimization-in-games-with-many-player-actions.
- Summary: Reran 3-iteration corrected-semantics CUDA probes with the new JSON
  telemetry. The fast default was badly under-fidelity: every chunk overflowed,
  mean pool demand was `3.98x`, and max demand was `8.38x`, although throughput
  was `367` traversals/sec. Raising slots to 1000 reduced mean demand to
  `1.76x` and max to `2.73x`, but every chunk still overflowed and throughput
  fell to `230` traversals/sec. The CUDA fork kernel currently demotes
  traverser nodes to sampled actions on pool exhaustion; that is a practical
  fallback, not a principled MCCFR sampling scheme.
- Commands: `uv run python scripts/poker_autoresearch_train.py --n-iterations 3 --n-traversals 4000 --n-training-steps 20 --hidden-dim 512 --n-layers 4 --batch-size 8192 --buffer-capacity 2000000 --save-dir autoresearch-session/corrected_allin_pool_telemetry_default_20260515 --prefix corrected_pool_default_3x4k --save-every 0 --eval-games 0`; `uv run python scripts/poker_autoresearch_train.py --n-iterations 3 --n-traversals 4000 --n-training-steps 20 --hidden-dim 512 --n-layers 4 --batch-size 8192 --buffer-capacity 2000000 --traversal-slots-per-traversal 1000 --save-dir autoresearch-session/corrected_allin_pool_telemetry_1000_20260515 --prefix corrected_pool1000_3x4k --save-every 0 --eval-games 0`
- Key metrics: `{"default_traversals_per_second": 367.371, "default_overflow_fraction": 1.0, "default_mean_pool_demand_ratio": 3.980049, "default_max_pool_demand_ratio": 8.375957, "slot1000_traversals_per_second": 229.765, "slot1000_overflow_fraction": 1.0, "slot1000_mean_pool_demand_ratio": 1.758695, "slot1000_max_pool_demand_ratio": 2.727944, "promotion": false}`
- Decision: Do not solve corrected traversal by more slot sweeps. The next
  principled direction is an algorithmic one: either stream full external
  sampling without fixed-pool demotion, or implement a published sampled-action
  MCCFR variant with proper importance weighting/variance controls.

## 20260515T114500Z-without-replacement-sampled-traversal - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T11:45:00Z
- Type: traversal_level_estimator_probe
- Gate: PPS without-replacement sampled-action estimator and tiny traversal
  check
- Hypothesis: Sampling traverser actions without replacement should avoid
  duplicate child evaluations, lower estimator variance, and preserve root
  action ordering better than the with-replacement sample-4 probe.
- Failure class: none
- Summary: Added exact inclusion-probability computation for the 9-action
  abstraction, a PPS without-replacement sampler, a Horvitz-Thompson sampled
  regret estimator, and a `--sampling-mode without-replacement` path for root
  and traversal diagnostics. The hard root estimator gate passed at sample-4
  with lower standard deviation than the with-replacement baseline. The tiny
  traversal probe preserved root top action on two seeds while retaining modest
  per-run speedups. This is still a research-only CPU diagnostic, but it is a
  cleaner candidate for CUDA traversal than with-replacement sample-4.
- Sources: MCCFR sampling framework https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2009/file/00411460f7c92d2124a67ea0f4cb5f85-Paper.pdf; VR-MCCFR baselines https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/4048; without-replacement estimators https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06043 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.09067

## 20260515T153000Z-sampled-traverser-action-pivot - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T15:30:00Z
- Type: estimator_protocol_review
- Gate: related-work check plus hard-seed 512-repeat variance check
- Hypothesis: The sample-4 priority-baseline failure might be a finite-sample
  artifact that disappears with more repeats.
- Failure class: estimator_contract_mismatch
- Related work: MCCFR external sampling samples chance/opponent actions while
  enumerating the updating player's legal actions; outcome sampling and
  external sampling both have regret bounds, but directly dropping updating
  player actions at the regret-target node is not the standard external
  sampling contract. Sources:
  https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/3713-monte-carlo-sampling-for-regret-minimization-in-extensive-games,
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.03057, and
  https://poker.cs.ualberta.ca/publications/NIPS12.pdf.
- Summary: Searched related MCCFR work and reran the hard seed with `512`
  repeats using the learned priority model as both priority and baseline. Bias
  dropped, but top-action agreement still failed. The method retained only a
  small speedup, so scaling repeats does not rescue the sampled-traverser-action
  direction as an acceleration path.
- Commands: `uv run python scripts/eval_sampled_deep_cfr_traversal_grid.py --seeds 20260527 --initial-chips-values 300 --n-repeats 512 --n-reference-repeats 512 --sample-count 4 --sampling-mode priority-without-replacement --priority-forced-count 2 --priority-source priority-model --priority-checkpoint autoresearch-session/restricted_value_baseline_xxl_seed20260524.pt --use-priority-baseline --hidden-dim 64 --n-layers 1 --min-top-match-rate 1.0 --min-mean-speedup 1.05 --max-mean-abs-bias 0.08 --require-all-top-match --max-case-mean-abs-bias 0.08 --output-json autoresearch-session/sampled_deep_cfr_traversal_grid_priority_model_baseline_xxl_f2_sample4_seed20260527_512rep_20260515.json`

## 20260515T111200Z-average-strategy-related-work-check - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T11:12:00Z
- Type: related_work
- Gate: Deep CFR / SD-CFR policy-deployment alignment check
- Hypothesis: The live large-pot calibration failure may come from deploying a
  single regret-derived policy rather than the average strategy object that
  Deep CFR theory and SD-CFR variants target.
- Failure class: none
- Summary: Related work supports the diagnosis. Deep CFR trains a separate
  policy network to approximate the weighted average strategy because the
  average strategy, not one iteration's instantaneous regret policy, is the
  equilibrium object. SD-CFR avoids average-policy-network approximation error
  by sampling among stored iteration value networks at trajectory start. ReBeL
  motivates aligning learning and search around public belief state values
  rather than isolated live subgame patches.
- Sources:
  - Deep CFR paper: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/brown19b/brown19b.pdf
  - SD-CFR paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07621
  - ReBeL / thesis discussion: https://www.csd.cmu.edu/sites/default/files/phd-thesis/CMU-CS-20-132.pdf
- Local check: `scripts/eval_sd_cfr_mixture.py` on retry-clean iteration 25/50
  vs incumbent produced mean `+119.7 chips/hand` but lower95 `-480.7`, so the
  tiny available checkpoint mixture is not promotable.
- Decision: Run a bounded GPU Deep CFR candidate with traversal-collected
  average-strategy targets and evaluate with `--strategy-source average-policy`.
  This is more principled than risk caps because it restores the Deep CFR
  deployed-object contract.

  A/B to fit temperature on source-heldout calibration records instead of the

  Source-heldout temperature was `3.9670`; calibrated external action log-lift
  became `+1.1111`, beating the current model by `+1.4033`. With the same
  calibration in range replay, disjoint-session true-range log-lift improved

## 20260515T183000Z-policy-only-rl-falsifier-decision-note

- Timestamp: 2026-05-15T18:30:00Z
- Type: research_decision_note
- Scale: decision note, not an experiment result or promotion claim.
- Summary: The PPO-policy discussion changes the next falsifier. A frozen neural
  policy can absorb public history and hidden-state inference implicitly and may
  be enough for policy execution. Public or latent belief is only strictly
  required when the engine wants online search/resolving to evaluate
  counterfactual hidden-state continuations. Therefore the most principled next
  step is a native full-deck 9-action policy-only PPO-style self-play falsifier
  with no resolver, no explicit opponent ranges, and no Slumbot-specific
  supervision. Compare the checkpoint against native NFSP/Deep CFR controls
  under duplicate-swapped H2H before spending live Slumbot hands.
- Decision: If the policy-only branch clears local controls with positive
  lower-bound evidence, simplify toward policy-only or game-theoretic RL. If it
  fails, return to learned latent public-belief/search with the failure recorded
  as evidence that policy execution alone is insufficient for the current goal.

- Failure class: belief_integration
- Related work: DeepStack/Supremus-style continual resolving uses learned counterfactual value estimates inside search, and ReBeL/Student of Games point to public-belief search units. The local lesson is the same: judge learned values by resolver behavior at the actual query boundary, not by detached per-state MAE alone.

Aggregated over all 96 no-projection roots, action agreement was `0.59375` and mean L1 was `0.64485`. This keeps aligned depth-limited resolving as the current most principled branch, but identifies zero-sum projection as a harmful or at least unproven integration transform at this scale.

## 20260516T012000Z-aligned-callback-leaf-cfr10-stability - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-16T01:20:00Z
- Type: depth_limited_resolving_contract
- Gate: callback-leaf-aligned-cfr10-stability
- Hypothesis: If the aligned learned-leaf branch is robust rather than a weak-CFR artifact, it should preserve root decisions under a stronger CFR10 callback distribution when train and inference queries are matched.
- Failure class: search_decision_alignment
- Related work: Depth-limited solving for imperfect-information games requires values at the public-belief/query boundary, and safe/nested subgame solving warns that local value changes must be judged by downstream strategy behavior. The local branch already predicts EV-style leaf values rather than raw CFV numerators; the remaining issue is decision impact, not only value scaling.
- Summary: A CFR5-trained `128/64` no-projection checkpoint passed the first CFR10 32-root check (`0.5625` agreement, `0.6440` mean L1) but failed the adjacent block (`0.5000`, `0.7805`). A matched CFR10 `64/32` contract also failed (`0.53125`, `0.7634`). Doubling the matched CFR10 training roots to `128` restored the primary 32-root pass (`0.59375`, `0.6981`), but the adjacent 32-root block failed on mean drift despite high top-action agreement (`0.6875`, `0.8050`). Across the two `128x32` CFR10 holdout blocks, agreement was `0.640625` and mean L1 was `0.75155`, just above the predeclared bound. A leaf-error-vs-root-drift audit found weak correlation between per-root leaf MAE and action L1 (`r=0.1166` for mean leaf MAE, `r=0.1109` for max leaf MAE), so supervised EV/CFV fit is not a reliable proxy for resolver safety. The next mechanism should target decision-aware value training, safe/multi-valued depth-limit integration, or search-impact labels rather than only scaling the same MSE objective.

## 20260516T013000Z-callback-leaf-structural-drift-predictor - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-16T01:30:00Z
- Type: decision_impact_diagnostic
- Gate: callback-leaf-cheap-drift-abstention
- Hypothesis: If learned-leaf failures are cheaply predictable, a structural drift predictor trained on one root-disjoint CFR10 block should identify high-drift roots on the adjacent block well enough to support exact fallback or selective replacement.
- Failure class: search_decision_alignment
- Related work: Safe and depth-limited solving papers justify fallback/safety mechanisms, but the fallback decision itself must be predictive; otherwise it becomes another benchmark-specific heuristic.
- Summary: Fitted a ridge predictor from deployable structural signals (`leaf_prediction_states`, prediction/solve time, callback calls, bet counts, legal count, actor/client position) on the `128..159` matched CFR10 block and tested on `160..191`. Train Pearson was `0.555`, but holdout Pearson collapsed to `-0.0068`, and holdout MAE was slightly worse than the train-mean constant (`0.3586` vs `0.3529`). Selective fallback by predicted drift did reduce mean L1 only because any exact fallback removes drift; it did not rank the highest-drift roots reliably. This falsifies a cheap structural abstention rule for the current data scale. The next useful step is a genuine search-impact target or safe/multi-valued depth-limit formulation, not a structural threshold.
- Metrics file: `autoresearch-session/depth_limited_contract_20260516/callback_leaf_aligned_iter10_leaf_drift_structural_predictor.json`

  or update trajectory, not simply "later is better" CFV substitution.

- Timestamp: 2026-05-21T13:41:48Z
- Type: methodology_note
- Gate: philosophy-audit
- Hypothesis: SD-CFR snapshot deployment is bitter-lesson aligned only if it reconstructs a predeclared average self-play strategy, not if it becomes post-hoc checkpoint ensembling.
- Failure class: none
- Summary: User flagged snapshot mixture as potentially suspicious. The clarified decision is to retire the phrase "checkpoint mixture" as a mainline objective and instead treat the target as **faithful average self-play strategy reconstruction**. This is principled when snapshots are stored according to a predeclared cadence, weighted by the algorithmic SD-CFR/linear-CFR contract, and sampled consistently for a trajectory. It is not principled if snapshots are selected or reweighted after local H2H/Slumbot outcomes. The current sparse four-checkpoint proxy remains diagnostic-only; the next clean experiment must predeclare cadence and weights before evaluation.

The selector uses only observable strategy, range-shape, action-drift, street, legality, and latency features; tests explicitly reject gates that improve strategy EV but harm selected-action EV. On real cross-trace EV artifacts, strategy-delta prediction signal was weak-positive (`r=0.432` confidence-to-noallin, `r=0.356` noallin-to-confidence), but selected-action EV was not learnable from the same summaries (`r=0.197` and `r=-0.360`). The stricter decision gate failed both ways. Confidence-to-noallin slightly improved mean strategy EV (`22.76` versus direct `19.77`) but worsened beat rate (`42.2%` versus `46.0%`) and kept selected-action EV negative. Noallin-to-confidence worsened both strategy EV and selected-action EV. Retire shallow observable trust gating; the next method needs an integrated latent/search-boundary objective, not a post-hoc selector.

- Hypothesis: The EV failure may be attributable to a simple observable relationship between response likelihood gain, strategy drift, range entropy, or action agreement and selected-action EV.
- Failure class: belief_integration
- Summary: Audited all four response-range EV artifacts. The failure is not explained by a simple likelihood or range-shape threshold. This supports the current causal model: the learned response signal improves private-hand likelihood but is not aligned with the resolver's action-value geometry.

## 20260521T211200Z-expanded-response-range-ev-replay-iter100 - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-21T21:12:00Z
- Type: diagnostic
- Gate: expanded cross-trace response-range counterfactual-EV replay
- Hypothesis: The 64-case positive mean EV signal should persist on a larger `iter100` fixed trace-state corpus if direct response-range replacement is a viable interface.
- Failure class: search_quality
- Summary: The larger 192-case replay falsified the optimistic 64-case mean. True-hand likelihood still improved, but mean strategy EV became slightly negative and only `32.3%` of states beat baseline. This strengthens the decision to retire direct response-range replacement and avoid threshold tuning; the next branch must integrate a learned latent/auxiliary response signal inside policy/search.

  segmented CUDA backend should preserve `torch-levelsync-cuda` root decisions

  satisfy the strict clean-run contract. The job completed on CUDA with usable
  throughput (`93.805` traversals/second, `84.425` iterations/hour), but failed
  because `traversal_rejected_chunks=4 > 0`; the rejected attempts represented
  `743` requested traversals and max rejected pool-demand ratio `1.122904`.

  pressure rather than accepted biased data, but the zero-rejection gate remains
  failed. The next fix is smaller initial chunks via higher
  `traversal_slots_per_traversal`, not only a larger pool.

## 20260522T175000Z-warm-start-gate-interpretation - mixed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-22T17:50:00Z
- Type: research_housekeeping
- Gate: decision-impact interpretation after warm-start resolver gate
- Hypothesis: The failed low-state regret/policy warm-start gate should be
  classified before another learned-search run, so the workflow does not keep
  tuning the same shallow interface.
- Failure class: search_quality
- Summary: The reviewed public-belief/search-state direction remains valid,
  but the current warm-start interface is not promotable. On 64 root-disjoint
  roots, learned warm-started CFR5 improved L1 only slightly over CFR5
  (`0.5091` vs `0.5255`), worsened KL (`0.2755` vs `0.2606`), reduced
  top-action agreement (`0.7031` vs `0.7656`), and lost clearly to uniform
  CFR10 (`0.3652` L1, `0.1266` KL, `0.8125` agreement) while costing about
  `2.68x` CFR5 latency. Per-root analysis found an oracle warm-vs-CFR10 choice
  could improve mean L1 to about `0.3105`, but that oracle is not deployable
  and prior shallow selectors overfit. The next mechanism must change the
  learned object: in-resolver closed-loop update learning, public-belief/search
  state consumed by solving, or exact GPU CFR frontier improvement.
- Metrics file: `autoresearch-session/search_consistency_restored200_100x2k_20260513/regret_policy_warm_start_lowstate_holdout64_with_cfr10_after_review_seed20260522.json`

  per millisecond if the update state can be learned; it does not validate the

## 20260522T182200Z-exact-backend-parity-after-hook-failures - mixed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-22T18:22:00Z
- Type: exact_search_acceleration_gate
- Gate: solver_backend_parity
- Hypothesis: After learned hook updates failed, exact GPU search acceleration
  should be preferred only if it preserves root decisions and improves latency
  on root-disjoint fixed public states.
- Failure class: search_quality
- Summary: The established `torch-levelsync-cuda` backend remains a useful
  exact-search accelerator versus CPU: on 8 root-disjoint turn states at CFR25
  it matched CPU top actions `8/8`, had zero illegal mass, and reduced mean
  latency from `8816 ms` to `160 ms` (`55.1x` speedup). It did not pass the
  ultra-strict dense-policy parity threshold because float32 recurrence drift
  gave mean L1 `0.00836` and max L1 `0.04015`, but the decision surface was
  stable. The newer `segmented-cuda` backend is not better on this shape: it
  matched `torch-levelsync-cuda` top actions `8/8` but was slower (`204 ms`
  versus `148 ms`) and had the same scale of policy drift. Keep
  `torch-levelsync-cuda` as the practical exact backend and do not promote

## 20260522T192700Z-search-target-versus-no-target-control - mixed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-22T19:27:00Z
- Type: decision_impact_gate
- Gate: search-target-versus-no-target-control-20260522T192700Z
- Hypothesis: If the CFR100 search-target auxiliary loss is useful, the
  25x2k search-target checkpoint should confidence-improve over a matched
  no-target 25x2k control, either through its regret source or its
  `policy-head-covered` deployment path.
- Failure class: insufficient_decision_impact
- Summary: The clean no-target control is weaker than the restored-history
  incumbent (`-801.1` chips/hand, lower95 `-1082.8`), matching the earlier
  observation that 25x2k candidates are short-budget controls rather than
  promotion candidates. Direct same-budget A/B is more informative: the
  search-target checkpoint's regret source beat the no-target control by
  `+65.2` chips/hand on average, and the `policy-head-covered` path beat it by
  `+46.1`, but both lower95 bounds were negative (`-111.9` and `-147.0`).
  This is a weak positive diagnostic, not reliable strength evidence. Do not
  tune search-target weight/count next; the next method step should be a

## 20260525T160000Z-per-iteration-in-resolver-warm-start-smoke - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-25T16:00:00Z
- Type: decision_impact_gate
- Gate: per-iteration selected-node solver-state warm-start smoke
- Hypothesis: Per-iteration selected-node solver-state targets should align the learned update model with the `iteration_update_fn` distribution better than a single static low-state warm-start target.
- Failure class: search_state_update_underfit
- Summary: Added `scripts/build_cfr_iteration_warm_start_targets.py` with a red-green unit test. The exporter created root-disjoint train/holdout datasets by repeating each selected public root across real CFR trace iterations and using current solver state as `low_*` input with CFR25 selected-node fields as the target. Export mechanics passed with no skipped roots (`8` train roots, `45,120` rows; `4` holdout roots, `22,560` rows). The first CUDA-trained low-state-aware model failed supervised holdout (`pred_policy` L1/KL `0.7959/1.7589` versus low-state `0.6150/0.3744`) and failed the actual in-resolver hook gate: hook-CFR5 L1/KL `1.0469/1.8812`, low CFR5 `0.7549/0.4315`, uniform CFR10 `0.5543/0.1947`, with hook top-action agreement `0.75` versus CFR10 `1.0` and zero illegal mass. This falsifies the tiny per-iteration field model as a useful search update and blocks hidden-size/loss-weight tuning from this smoke. The exporter remains useful as a diagnostic surface only if the next candidate changes the learned object substantially or scales under a predeclared root-disjoint review.

## 20260525T160826Z-bounded-regret-residual-hook-smoke - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-25T16:08:26Z
- Type: decision_impact_gate
- Gate: bounded regret residual in-resolver hook smoke
- Hypothesis: A learned search update should add a bounded legal residual in the current CFR regret/advantage geometry, rather than replacing selected-node strategy or regret fields outright, and this should move root decisions closer to a CFR25 reference than low CFR5 or uniform CFR10.
- Failure class: search_state_update_misalignment
- Summary: Added `scripts/eval_bounded_regret_residual_hook.py` and `test/unit/test_bounded_regret_residual_hook.py`. The unit test confirms the updater preserves legal support and caps per-hand residual mass. The held-out root-disjoint gate still failed decisively. On cases `192:196`, the bounded hook remained legal (`max_hook_illegal_mass=0.0`) but produced worse root distributions than both low CFR5 and uniform CFR10: hook L1/KL `1.0465/1.8779`, low CFR5 `0.7549/0.4315`, and CFR10 `0.5543/0.1947`. Hook top-action agreement was `0.75` versus CFR10 `1.0`, and hook latency was higher than CFR10. This falsifies the current learned-hook family at smoke scale. Do not tune residual cap, hidden size, or epochs next; the active goal's stop condition is reached unless a principled pivot is approved.

- Timestamp: 2026-05-25T19:29Z
- Type: mechanism_gate
- Gate: manual held-out root fit, early-street calibration, fixed-continuation rollout, and matched no-target H2H for mixed external-plus-traversal average-policy actor
- Hypothesis: Mixing exact-search external average-policy targets with traversal-collected average-strategy memory should preserve whole-game coverage, repair the external-only early-street over-jam collapse, and improve same-budget decision transfer.
- Failure class: strategy_quality

- Summary: The mixed actor fixed the most obvious pathology from the external-only pilot. Early-street top all-in rate dropped from `0.5957` to `0.0352` overall, and preflop/flop top all-in rates dropped to `0.0331/0.0381`. Held-out root fit remained better than the no-target control (`1.0533` mean L1 and `1.2518` KL versus control `1.4962/12.6582`) with higher top1 match (`0.3828`). Fixed-continuation rollout showed a large remaining oracle gap (`60.3` chips; oracle match `0.0781`). The failure is no longer mainly coverage/all-in collapse; it is that supervised average-policy target matching does not choose high-value actions under the whole-game continuation.

- Hypothesis: Replacing cross-entropy mirror-target fitting with a KL-anchored expected-Q actor objective should reduce action collapse and pass the fixed-root decision-impact gate.
- Failure class: strategy_quality
- Related work: The test follows the regularized policy-improvement interpretation from Expert Iteration, regularized MCTS policy optimization, NeuRD, and Student of Games: optimize value improvement under a prior/trust-region constraint rather than only imitate a target policy.
- Summary: Added per-action search-value payloads to the on-policy decision-value collector, a `DecisionValueQTargetBuffer`, and a `--actor-update kl-q` path that trains the policy head with `E_pi[Q_search] - beta KL(pi || pi_base)`. Unit tests verify Q-target construction, metadata coverage, and that the KL-Q objective improves on a controlled target. The matched smoke was mechanically valid (`18` targets; street counts `{"0": 12, "1": 4, "2": 1, "3": 1}`; coverage passed) and the training objective improved (`expected_q -0.137 -> -0.063`, KL to base `7.651 -> 4.771`). This is less bad than the CE version (`-2.32` policy EV) but not a pass. Do not tune `kl_beta` or hidden size next; the evidence points to the post-hoc policy-head interface being too weak/out-of-distribution.

Unit tests verify that the collector can use the search-improved target as the actual behavior action and records behavior actions in target metadata. Greedy search-improved behavior produced more diverse collected behavior (`all_in:3, call:5, fold:4, raise_1.0:4, raise_1.5:2`) and improved fixed-root selected-action value more than the post-hoc KL-Q run (`12.5 -> 42.09`) while reducing oracle gap (`208.19 -> 178.60`). It still failed because policy EV regressed (`14.71 -> 0.65`) and the policy selected mostly `raise_1.0` (`14/16`). Sampling from the search-improved target was worse: selected-action value fell to `-19.53`, policy EV to `-2.82`, and oracle gap increased to `240.22`. The search-improved trajectory idea is more promising than post-hoc labels, but the current covered policy-head overlay remains the bottleneck.
- Metrics file: `autoresearch-session/decision_value_actor/restored_search_improved_behavior_kl_q_policy_head_smoke.json` and `autoresearch-session/decision_value_actor/restored_search_improved_sample_behavior_kl_q_policy_head_smoke.json`

- Decision: Keep `frontier-live` non-default until live transfer is measured. Use it for exact resolving latency/transfer smokes or as the teacher frontier that learned resolver updates must beat.

## 20260526T151707Z-frontier-live-slumbot-transfer-smoke - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-26T15:17:07Z
- Type: slumbot_transfer_smoke
- Gate: frontier-live-exact-cuda-resolving-100h-noallin
- Hypothesis: If CFR125 exact CUDA resolving is locally close to the CFR150 teacher, then the opt-in `frontier-live` profile should improve or at least not destabilize Slumbot no-all-in transfer versus prior fast/live profiles.
- Failure class: weak_transfer
- Summary: Ran a 100-hand no-all-in Slumbot smoke with `--solver-backend torch-levelsync-cuda --solver-budget-profile frontier-live`. The run was mechanically clean with no API/parse/fallback errors, and CUDA was visible but bursty. Transfer was negative and high variance: several risk hands and solver/policy interactions produced stack-scale losses. This is not promotion evidence and does not justify making `frontier-live` default.
- Metrics files: `autoresearch-session/slumbot_traces/frontier_live_noallin_100h_20260526.jsonl`, `autoresearch-session/slumbot_trace_audits/frontier_live_noallin_100h_20260526.json`
- Key metrics: `avg_chips_per_hand=-556.06`, `solver_decisions=39`, `policy_decisions=138`, `big_losses=7`, `stack_losses=3`, mean solver latency `1126.7 ms`, max solver latency `1573.3 ms`.
- Related work checked: DeepStack/continual resolving, Libratus safe and nested subgame solving (`https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.02955`), ReBeL (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13544`), and Student of Games (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03178`) all support resolving/search as a principled operator, but only when it is calibrated to the deployed belief and continuation distribution.
- Decision: Keep exact CUDA resolving as a teacher/frontier, not a deployment claim. The next diagnostic is trace-derived response/range counterfactual EV replay on the failed live trace, judged by decision EV rather than chip-noisy 100-hand results.

## 20260526T152055Z-response-range-ev-replay-frontier-trace - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-26T15:20:55Z
- Type: mechanism_gate
- Gate: frontier-live-trace-response-range-counterfactual-ev
- Hypothesis: If failed frontier-live transfer is mainly caused by miscalibrated Slumbot response beliefs, then response-conditioned trace ranges should both improve revealed-hand/action likelihood and improve selected-action EV under the counterfactual replay gate.
- Failure class: likelihood_not_decision_value
- Summary: Built 39 resolver cases from the failed 100-hand frontier-live trace, scored Slumbot action likelihoods, and compared response-conditioned resolver decisions against the baseline. The response model strongly improved revealed-hand likelihood, but this did not translate into better decisions. Selected-action and strategy EV deltas were negative, so explicit response range replacement is rejected as a deployable mechanism.
- Metrics files: `autoresearch-session/slumbot_trace_cases/frontier_live_noallin_100h_20260526_cases.json`, `autoresearch-session/slumbot_trace_cases/frontier_live_noallin_100h_20260526_action_likelihood.json`, `autoresearch-session/slumbot_trace_cases/frontier_live_noallin_100h_20260526_opponent_response_baseline.json`, `autoresearch-session/slumbot_trace_cases/frontier_live_noallin_100h_20260526_response_range_ev.json`
- Key metrics: `n_evaluated=39`, `true_hand_response_beats_baseline_rate=0.9487`, `mean_selected_action_ev_delta=-715.61`, `mean_strategy_ev_delta=-129.44`, `response_selected_action_ev_beats_baseline_rate=0.2564`, `ev_gate_passed=false`, `promotable=false`.
- Related work checked: Data-Augmented Game Starts (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14379`) motivates using hard states as training starts instead of post-hoc range patches; VRPO (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19235`) motivates variance-reduced value/advantage updates over terminal-return cloning; ReBeL and Student of Games still favor search coupled to learning rather than detached likelihood fixes.
- Decision: Do not tune response ranges or run more Slumbot from this branch. The next bounded branch is a DAGS-style trace-start/self-play contract: turn failed live trace states into a principled training distribution with explicit source/context flags, then test whether a search-guided or Q-boosted RL update improves held-out root decisions and local league strength.

It intentionally reports a promotion blocker because this is not yet a playable environment start.

The next implementation should prefer a feature-level hard-state update or a continuous-bet trace-state contract before native `PokerState` restarts; the 21 soft-mapped bets show that naive replay through the 9-action environment would silently change part of the game.

## 20260526T153713Z-trace-start-policy-head-probe - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-26T15:37:13Z
- Type: mechanism_gate
- Gate: trace-start-feature-level-policy-head
- Hypothesis: If failed Slumbot trace states contain reusable decision signal, then a small neural policy head trained on verified trace-start features and counterfactual action values should improve held-out selected-action EV over the baseline action.
- Failure class: generalization_mismatch
- Summary: Added `poker_ai.research.trace_start_policy` and `scripts/train_trace_start_policy_head.py` to train a diagnostic policy head on trace-start features with a source flag. A one-trace split overfit: train selected-action EV improved, but held-out selected-action EV regressed despite positive held-out oracle EV. A multi-trace leave-frontier-out probe repeated the failure more strongly: train traces improved, but the held-out frontier trace regressed badly.
- Metrics files: `autoresearch-session/slumbot_trace_cases/frontier_live_noallin_100h_20260526_trace_policy_probe.json`, `autoresearch-session/slumbot_trace_cases/multitrace_holdout_frontier_trace_policy_probe_20260526.json`
- Key metrics: single-trace train selected-action EV delta `+410.99`, held-out selected-action EV delta `-212.57`, held-out oracle EV delta `+172.32`; multi-trace leave-frontier-out train selected-action EV delta `+427.54`, held-out selected-action EV delta `-831.23`, held-out oracle EV delta `+325.56`, held-out selected actions did not collapse (`6` distinct actions).
- Related work checked: Data-Augmented Game Starts (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14379`) supports hard-state starts but as a distribution for self-play exploration, not one-trace supervised fitting; VRPO (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19235`) supports variance-reduced RL updates; Student of Games (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03178`) supports learning from many search/self-play contexts.
- Validation: `pytest -q test/unit/test_trace_start_policy.py` passed; synthesis and innovation reviews passed with decision `revise/proceed`.
- Decision: Do not promote feature-level trace policy fitting and do not run Slumbot from it. The next principled branch should either build a continuous-bet/replayable trace-state contract or consume hard states inside a variance-reduced in-resolver/self-play update, with leave-trace-out decision EV as the gate.

## 20260526T170039Z-true-replay-continuation-local-h2h - failed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-26T17:00:39Z
- Type: experiment
- Failure class: strategy_quality
- Summary: Ran a modest replay-backed parent-child GPU Deep CFR continuation A/B. The first parent attempt failed the fidelity gate with two rejected traversal chunks; rerunning with `--traversal-slots-per-traversal 16000` passed. The first child also failed with rejected chunks; rerunning with `--traversal-slots-per-traversal 24000` passed and hard-restored replay state. Internal duplicate-swapped H2H then rejected the child: true continuation was mechanically valid, but this small extra training step made the policy much worse than its parent.
- Metrics files: `autoresearch-session/replay_continuation_scaled_20260526/replay_parent_3x256_slots16000_metrics.json`, `autoresearch-session/replay_continuation_scaled_20260526/replay_child_3x256_slots24000_metrics.json`, `autoresearch-session/replay_continuation_scaled_20260526/child_vs_parent_h2h_300x3.json`
- Key metrics: `{"parent_passed": true, "parent_iteration": 3, "parent_replay_n_seen": [286769, 1046149], "child_passed": true, "child_resume_semantics": "true_replay_buffer_continuation", "child_iteration": 6, "child_replay_n_seen": [683952, 2560575], "h2h_avg_chips_per_hand": -921.5194, "h2h_lower95_chips_per_hand": -1201.21}`
- Interpretation: This is not Slumbot evidence and not a final rejection of Deep CFR scaling. It does falsify the immediate assumption that a small true replay continuation automatically improves the local self-play policy. The next continuation should either run a larger, properly checkpointed training curve with intermediate league checkpoints, or pivot to a self-play objective that tracks average-strategy quality directly rather than relying on short child-vs-parent regret-source snapshots.

## 20260526T181000Z-alphazero-style-neural-self-play-policy-iteration-decision-note

- Timestamp: 2026-05-26T18:10:00Z
- Type: research_decision_note
- Scale: direction-setting note, not a promotion claim.
- Hypothesis: The next mainline should be closer to AlphaZero-style neural
  self-play policy iteration than to a traditional poker bot that simply runs
  CFR online. The neural network should be the stochastic player used
  throughout self-play; public-belief CFR/resolving should act as a policy
  improvement operator and training target, not as a deterministic live policy
  replacement.
- Related work:
  - AlphaZero replaces handcrafted evaluation and move heuristics with a
    policy/value network trained from self-play and search targets; the network
    then guides future search. Source: Silver et al. Science 2018,
    https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aar6404.
  - ReBeL explicitly generalizes the self-play RL plus search paradigm to
    imperfect-information games through public-belief states, and reports
    superhuman HUNL performance with less domain knowledge than prior poker AI.
    Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13544.
  - Student of Games reinforces the same pattern: self-play generates full-game
    trajectories and search queries for value/policy networks, combining guided
    search, learning, and game-theoretic reasoning. Source:
    https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03178.
  - NFSP is useful as a warning and baseline: it combines fictitious self-play
    with deep RL and reports that common RL methods diverged in Leduc poker.
    Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01121.
  - Recent policy-gradient work argues PPO-style methods deserve serious
    imperfect-information controls, especially when regularized toward Nash
    dynamics. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08938 and
    https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00751.
  - Gymnasium, PettingZoo, and RLCard are useful environment/API scaffolds for
    reproducible self-play controls; Rainbow/PPO are useful RL baselines, but
    they are not by themselves the final philosophy. Sources:
    https://gymnasium.farama.org/, https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.14471,
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.04376, and https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.02298.
- Summary: The preferred research story is now: neural stochastic policy plays
  full hands in local self-play; public-belief CFR improves selected states into
  stronger mixed strategies; the neural policy/value network trains on those
  improved mixed strategies and self-play outcomes; the updated network returns
  to self-play and should need less online search over time. CFR remains
  allowed because poker needs equilibrium-aware improvement, but the engine
  should not become "always run fixed-budget CFR and argmax." Always choosing a
  deterministic best action is exploitable; deployed policies should remain
  stochastic unless a reviewed gate proves otherwise.
- Decision: Reframe the next mainline as neural self-play policy iteration with
  public-belief CFR as the improvement operator. The current strategy-vector
  selector is a useful local diagnostic, but not enough. The next implementation
  should make the neural policy/value network more central: collect self-play
  trajectories from the stochastic neural policy, run CFR improvement on sampled
  states, train the policy/value heads on search-improved mixed strategies and
  outcomes, and validate by root-disjoint exact-CFR gates plus self-play league
  lower bounds before any Slumbot held-out evaluation.

- Type: implementation_performance_falsifier
- Scale: 16 local self-play turn/river CFR5 teacher targets; systems

- Related-work note: AlphaZero-style systems scale by coupling self-play,
  search, and neural training in parallel; Student of Games extends that idea
  to imperfect-information games by combining guided search, self-play
  learning, and game-theoretic reasoning. The local mechanism remains aligned:
  the neural policy is the actor and CFR is only the local improvement teacher.
- Hypothesis: Same-topology batched torch-levelsync CFR can raise useful GPU
  work inside the public-belief CFR teacher when local self-play produces
  repeated turn/river solver shapes.
- Summary: Added opt-in `cfr_batch_roots` / `cfr_batch_min_roots` to the NPI
  CFR teacher and CLI. The teacher now groups exact same-topology roots,
  includes hand count in the topology key, solves eligible groups through
  `solve_cfr_levelsync_torch_batched_same_topology`, falls back to serial
  solves for singleton or failed groups, and reports context/solve timing:
  `solver_context_sec`, `serial_solver_sec`, `batched_solver_sec`,
  `batched_solver_roots`, and `batched_solver_failures`.
- Metrics files:
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/cfr_teacher16_cfr5_batched_cuda_h64_seed20260572.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/cfr_teacher16_cfr5_serial_cuda_h64_seed20260572.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/cfr_teacher16_cfr5_instrumented_serial_cuda_h64_seed20260572.json`
- Key metrics: `{"targets": 16, "batched_roots": 11, "batched_groups": 1, "batched_failures": 0, "batch_teacher_target_sec": 5.6230, "instrumented_serial_teacher_target_sec": 5.6834, "batch_solver_context_sec": 5.4091, "batch_batched_solver_sec": 0.0772, "batch_serial_solver_sec": 0.1357, "instrumented_serial_solver_context_sec": 5.4064, "instrumented_serial_solver_sec": 0.2757, "training_sec": 0.4468, "promotion": false}`
- Decision: Batched CFR recurrence works and avoids the prior topology bug, but
  it does not yet improve wall-clock. The dominant cost is constructing
  per-board solver contexts and terminal matrices (`~5.4s` of `~5.6s` teacher
  time), not the CFR recurrence (`~0.21-0.28s`). The next compute-aligned step
  should target solver-context/terminal-matrix construction, a ragged/fused
  terminal evaluator, or denser self-play targets that avoid building a full
  one-off street solver per target. Do not scale this batching hook alone as a
  strength path.

  not strength, Slumbot, SOTA, or promotion evidence.

  a neural policy/value network as the actor (`https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.01815`).
  ReBeL and Student of Games motivate the imperfect-information adaptation:
  use public-belief/game-theoretic search as the improvement operator while the
  neural policy learns from self-play (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13544`,
  `https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03178`). Deep CFR remains the nearest poker
  precedent for neural approximation of regret/self-play signals
  (`https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.00164`).
- Hypothesis: The project needs a repeatable checkpoint-to-checkpoint neural
  policy-iteration loop before judging whether the AlphaZero/RL philosophy
  translates to poker.
- Summary: Added `initial_checkpoint_path` / CLI `--checkpoint-in` to
  `run_neural_policy_iteration_pilot.py`, saving `parent_checkpoint_path` and
  metrics that identify whether the actor was initialized from a parent
  checkpoint. Added `scripts/run_neural_policy_iteration_loop.py`, which runs
  generation `N`, feeds its checkpoint into generation `N+1`, and evaluates
  `N+1` versus `N` with the duplicate-swapped local H2H gate. No Slumbot data is
  used.
- Metrics files:
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/az_loop_smoke_20260526/summary.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/az_loop_smoke_20260526/public_world_gate_gen0.json`,

- Decision: Infrastructure is now philosophically cleaner: the neural network

## 20260526T214500Z-plugin-rl-and-dueling-nfsp-control - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-26T21:45:00Z
- Type: rl_framework_control_and_native_capacity_probe
- Scale: RLCard NFSP 20-episode framework smoke; native full-deck 9-action NFSP
  100-episode matched MLP versus dueling-DDQN smoke; 1k duplicate-swapped H2H.
  This is not Slumbot, SOTA, or promotion evidence.
- Related work: NFSP is the poker-relevant game-theoretic RL wrapper because it
  combines best-response learning with average-policy fictitious self-play
  (`https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01121`, `https://proceedings.mlr.press/v37/heinrich15`).
  Rainbow is a bundle of DQN improvements, including Double DQN and dueling
  networks, but it is not by itself an equilibrium method
  (`https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.02298`, `https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.06581`,
  `https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.06461`).
- Hypothesis: If the neural learner is too weak, the most aligned first probe
  is a stronger Q learner inside the NFSP average-policy wrapper, plus
  plug-and-play external RL controls, rather than adding poker-specific
  anti-collapse rules.
- Summary: Fixed the RLCard NFSP wrapper so tiny plug-and-play framework
  controls clamp RLCard supervised and Q replay batch sizes to the replay init
  size; the previous smoke failed inside RLCard DQN sampling with "Sample larger
  than population". Added an opt-in native `--q-network-arch dueling` Q head for
  full-deck 9-action NFSP. The default remains MLP. The native Q target was
  already Double-DQN style: the online Q network selects the best next action
  and the target Q network evaluates it. An ephemeral `uv run --with tianshou`
  import check succeeded with Tianshou `2.0.1` and found the stable
  `RainbowDQN` API, so a future plug-in Rainbow control should use Tianshou
  rather than a local Rainbow reimplementation.
- Metrics files:
  `autoresearch-session/framework_controls/rlcard_nfsp_smoke_20260526.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/native_nfsp_rainbow/seed20260526_mlp.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/native_nfsp_rainbow/seed20260526_dueling.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/native_nfsp_rainbow/dueling_vs_mlp_h2h_1k_seed20260526.json`
- Key metrics: `{"rlcard_num_actions": 5, "rlcard_train_episodes": 20, "rlcard_q_batch_size": 8, "rlcard_resolved_device": "cpu", "native_mlp_episodes_per_second": 70.9213, "native_dueling_episodes_per_second": 64.3184, "native_mlp_eval_vs_random": 0.05298, "native_dueling_eval_vs_random": 0.06715, "dueling_vs_mlp_h2h_mean": -0.038309, "dueling_vs_mlp_h2h_lower95": -0.061574, "promotion": false}`
- Verification: `uv run pytest -q test/unit/test_native_nfsp_pilot.py test/unit/test_rlcard_nfsp_pilot.py` passed (`19 passed`).
- Decision: The plug-and-play path is now usable for framework controls, but
  RLCard remains a 5-action abstraction and cannot promote a Slumbot-parity
  checkpoint. The dueling Q head is a clean Rainbow-style capacity control
  inside NFSP, but the first matched H2H is negative, so it should not be scaled
  without a materially stronger library-backed algorithm or a native-league gate
  that beats MLP NFSP. The active AlphaZero-style NPI branch remains the main
  path; external RL algorithms should enter as controls or as learners wrapped
  by native self-play league evaluation.

## 20260526T221000Z-tianshou-native-rainbow-control - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-26T22:10:00Z
- Type: plug_in_rl_control
- Scale: Tianshou RainbowDQN single-agent control, native full-deck 9-action
  observation and legal mask, random local opponent, 256 collected train steps,
  3 updates, 20 random-opponent eval games on CUDA. This is not self-play
  equilibrium evidence, Slumbot evidence, or promotion evidence.
- Related work: Rainbow combines DQN improvements such as distributional value
  learning, multi-step returns, prioritized replay, noisy/dueling-style
  exploration/capacity, and target-network stabilization
  (`https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.02298`). Tianshou exposes the current
  `RainbowDQN` API (`https://tianshou.org/en/stable/03_api/algorithm/modelfree/rainbow.html`).
  NFSP remains the more poker-relevant wrapper for equilibrium pressure
  (`https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01121`).
- Hypothesis: If the current neural network is too weak, a plug-in Rainbow
  control should be tested before hand-implementing value-learning variants.
- Summary: Added `scripts/run_tianshou_rainbow_native_control.py`. The wrapper
  exposes the repo's 9-action full-deck state as a Gymnasium observation dict
  with `obs` and legal `mask`, uses Tianshou `C51Policy` + `RainbowDQN`, and
  saves a diagnostic checkpoint. The first CUDA attempt exposed a framework
  boundary bug: Tianshou's C51 support tensor stayed on CPU while the model ran
  on CUDA. Moving the whole policy to the resolved device fixed the issue. The
  script also supports duplicate-swapped H2H against a native NFSP average
  policy checkpoint via `--checkpoint-in ... --baseline-checkpoint ...`.
- Metrics file:
  `autoresearch-session/tianshou_rainbow/native_random_smoke_20260527.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/tianshou_rainbow/rainbow_vs_native_nfsp_mlp_h2h_200_seed20260528.json`
- Key metrics: `{"train_steps": 256, "updates": 3, "resolved_device": "cuda", "train_steps_per_second": 163.4143, "mean_eval_payoff_p0_vs_random": -0.1375, "last_loss": 3.9083, "h2h_vs_native_mlp_nfsp_mean": -0.13061, "h2h_vs_native_mlp_nfsp_lower95": -0.154061, "promotion": false, "league_eligible": false}`
- Verification: `uv run --with tianshou pytest -q test/unit/test_tianshou_rainbow_native_control.py` passed; `uv run pytest -q test/unit/test_tianshou_rainbow_native_control.py` passed with the Tianshou smoke skipped when the optional dependency is absent.
- Decision: This validates a plug-in RL control surface without reimplementing
  Rainbow locally, but the first random-opponent and local-H2H smokes are
  negative. Do not promote or scale it as a mainline method. The next useful RL
  step would need a native self-play/equilibrium wrapper that improves local
  league strength; otherwise continue the AlphaZero-style NPI/search-improvement
  branch.

## 20260526T223500Z-npi-target-collapse-gate - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-26T22:35:00Z
- Type: workflow_gate_hardening
- Scale: Unit test plus tiny one-generation NPI loop smoke with strict
  `--max-target-top-action-fraction 0.5`; four legal-mixed teacher targets all
  chose the same top action. This is a guardrail validation, not strength
  evidence.
- Related work: AlphaZero-style policy improvement trains the network on search
  distributions, but deployment quality depends on those targets not collapsing
  into a brittle deterministic action distribution. NFSP/Deep CFR likewise rely
  on averaged or distributional strategy targets rather than one lucky argmax
  (`https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.01815`, `https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01121`,
  `https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.00164`).
- Hypothesis: The NPI loop should be able to fail fast when the teacher target
  set is dominated by one top action, because prior NPI runs showed all-in/call
  collapse could pass tiny H2H while worsening fixed-root decisions.
- Summary: Added `max_target_top_action_fraction` to
  `NeuralPolicyIterationConfig`, `run_neural_policy_iteration_pilot.py`, and
  `run_neural_policy_iteration_loop.py`. The default `1.0` preserves existing
  behavior; autoresearch runs can set a stricter threshold such as `0.75`. The
  pilot now appends a gate failure when `max_target_top_action_fraction` exceeds
  the configured bound, and the loop propagates that failure through top-level
  `passed=false`.
- Metrics file:
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/collapse_gate_smoke_20260526/summary.json`
- Key metrics: `{"improvement_targets": 4, "target_top_action_counts": {"1": 4}, "max_target_top_action_fraction": 1.0, "threshold": 0.5, "exit_code": 1, "promotion": false}`
- Verification: `uv run pytest -q test/unit/test_neural_policy_iteration.py -k 'fails_on_target_top_action_collapse or loop_cli_writes_generations or positive_league_gate or compares_each_generation_to_controls'` passed; the command-line collapse smoke returned `EXIT_CODE=1` as intended.
- Decision: This does not improve playing strength by itself, but it prevents
  the current AlphaZero-style loop from treating collapsed teacher targets as a
  valid improvement step. Future NPI runs should include a nontrivial
  `--max-target-top-action-fraction` alongside control-checkpoint gates.

  need distributional/self-play safeguards so a search-improved target does not
  collapse into a brittle policy (`https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.01815`,
  `https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01121`, `https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13544`).
- Hypothesis: A dense public-world teacher plus inverse top-action weighting

  the fixed smoke control with positive confidence (`mean=+0.052544`,
  lower95 `+0.024640`) but failed to beat gen0 (`mean=-0.005715`, lower95
