## 20260526T232500Z-npi-all-state-value-training-contract - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-26T23:25:00Z
- Type: alpha_zero_style_contract_fix
- Scale: Unit tests plus cheap legal-mixed NPI smoke. This is a workflow/model
  contract correction, not poker-strength evidence.
- Hypothesis: The NPI trainer should not train the value network only on the
  subset of states that receive search-improved policy targets. AlphaZero-style
  policy iteration learns value from the whole self-play trajectory while policy
  targets may be generated by search at selected decision states.
- Summary: `_train_on_policy_improvement_targets` now accepts
  `value_samples`; `run_neural_policy_iteration_pilot` passes all collected
  self-play samples to value training while keeping policy loss restricted to
  selected search/improvement targets. Metrics now report
  `policy_training_samples` and `value_training_samples`. Target diagnostics
  also report top-action counts and max top-action fraction by street.
- Metrics file:
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/all_state_value_training_smoke_20260526.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/public_belief_cfr_coverage_probe_20260526/summary_by_street.json`

## 20260526T233000Z-plug-in-game-framework-check - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-26T23:30:00Z
- Type: related_work_and_framework_control
- Scale: Online related-work check plus ephemeral `uv run --with open-spiel`
  import probe. This is research/workflow evidence, not training evidence.
- Related work: OpenSpiel documents AlphaZero as self-play plus MCTS using a
  neural prior/value model, while warning its public implementation is an
  illustrative reimplementation rather than the original challenge-match code
  (`https://openspiel.readthedocs.io/en/latest/alpha_zero.html`). Student of
  Games reports a unified self-play/search/game-theoretic system that reaches
  strong performance in both perfect- and imperfect-information games, including
  heads-up no-limit Texas Hold'em
  (`https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10651118/`). ReBeL and related
  poker search work support the same principle: learned values/policies must be
  consumed inside search, not trained as detached diagnostics.
- Probe: `uv run --with open-spiel python - ...` installed/imported
  `open-spiel==1.6.15`, confirmed `universal_poker` is registered, and found
  packaged algorithms including `alpha_zero`, `cfr`, `discounted_cfr`, `mccfr`,
  and MCTS variants. `universal_poker` defaulted to a small 4-action imperfect
  information poker game, so it is a framework/reference control unless wrapped
  into the repo's Slumbot-parity 9-action abstraction.
- Decision: The user's reminder is correct: do not hand-implement generic RL
  algorithms when maintained libraries can serve as controls. Use Tianshou and
  OpenSpiel for plug-in baselines/reference behavior where they match the
  experiment. The main project contribution should remain the native
  Slumbot-parity self-play/search workflow and especially wiring learned value
  into the policy-improvement/search loop.

  (`https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10651118/`).

  `-0.018599`). The prior-guided version, which combines learned one-step
  public-world values with the current stochastic actor prior, passed the target
  gate (`{"1": 105, "7": 151}`, max fraction `0.589844`) and parent H2H
  (`mean=+0.009827`, lower95 `+0.001455`). Its initial 1k fixed-control H2H was
  neutral, but a 5k rerun passed with `mean=+0.005018`, lower95 `+0.001282`,
  upper95 `+0.008753`.

- Decision: This is meaningful progress but not SOTA evidence. The first

  diagnostic shows that both policies still lose EV under their mixed policy

- Scale: Same one-generation sampled-state value-prior NPI loop with seed
  `20260597`, then held-out public-world roots with seed `20260598` and
  exact-CFR roots with seed `20260599`.
- Summary: The local signal reproduced. The target set again covered all

  state-value targets, had zero fallbacks, and passed the target-collapse gate
  (`max_target_top_action_fraction=0.710938`). It beat the fixed control in the

  expected stochastic policy EV also improved (`9.6331` vs control `8.0471`),

  vs `0.2528`), but top-action agreement stayed `0.0625` and policy top action

  interface: either the policy should be evaluated and consumed as a stochastic
  mixed strategy end-to-end, or the policy-improvement teacher must train a
  decisively better mixed distribution rather than only nudging probability mass
  while argmax stays collapsed to call.

### Two-generation loop update

- Scale: Two-generation sampled-state value-prior NPI loop from the fixed smoke
  control, seed `20260600`, same 256-target/32-step/h32 budget and 1k
  duplicate-swapped league gates.
- Summary: The iterative self-play claim is partially supported but not
  promotable. Gen0 passed the target-collapse gate (`0.746094`) and beat the
  initial checkpoint (`mean=+0.037989`, lower95 `+0.020382`) as well as the
  fixed control (`mean=+0.035110`, lower95 `+0.016810`). Gen1 beat gen0
  (`mean=+0.013971`, lower95 `+0.001402`) and also beat the fixed control
  (`mean=+0.050553`, lower95 `+0.029918`), so stochastic local league strength
  did improve across generations. The run still failed because gen1's target
  distribution collapsed to call: `223/256` targets had action `1` as top
  action, giving `max_target_top_action_fraction=0.871094`.
- Metrics file:
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/sampled_state_value_prior_2gen_20260526/summary_h32_seed20260600.json`
- Key metrics: `{"gen0_lower95_vs_parent": 0.020382, "gen1_lower95_vs_gen0": 0.001402, "gen1_lower95_vs_fixed": 0.029918, "gen1_max_target_top_action_fraction": 0.871094, "passed": false, "promotion": false}`
- Decision: This is the strongest evidence so far that the AlphaZero-like local
  self-play loop can make repeatable stochastic policy improvements in the
  native 9-action game. It is still blocked by teacher-policy collapse and
  root-action calibration. Do not lower the collapse gate and do not run
  Slumbot. The next principled step is to change the improvement target so it
  stays a stable mixed strategy across generations, using general search/RL
  mechanisms or plug-in baselines rather than hand-coded action caps.
- Workflow note: Generic RL algorithms are control/reference tools, not
  infrastructure to reimplement by hand. Prefer plug-in libraries such as
  Tianshou, RLCard, OpenSpiel, or stable-baselines-style PPO/Rainbow/NFSP
  surfaces when they can be wrapped around the native 9-action game; only write
  local code for the poker-specific observation/action adapter, evaluator, and
  promotion gates.

## 20260527T011500Z-plug-in-rainbow-control-rerun - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-27T01:15:00Z
- Type: plug_in_rl_control_falsifier
- Scale: Tianshou Rainbow DQN control on the native 9-action full-deck
  single-agent Gymnasium wrapper, CUDA model device, 10,240 collected env
  steps, 16 learner updates, hidden dim 256, batch 512, 100 random-opponent
  eval games, then 500 duplicate-swapped H2H games against the existing native
  NFSP h512 10k checkpoint. No Slumbot data was used.
- Related work: Tianshou exposes modular PyTorch RL algorithms including
  Rainbow/PPO (`https://tianshou.org/en/stable/`), so generic RL controls
  should use plug-in algorithms rather than local reimplementations. NFSP
  remains the imperfect-information RL reference because the original paper
  found common RL methods diverged in Leduc poker while NFSP approached Nash
  (`https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01121`). ReBeL/AlphaZero-style work still
  argues for coupling self-play, search, and learned value/policy in poker
  (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13544`).
- Hypothesis: A stronger off-the-shelf Rainbow control might show that the
  current bottleneck is only weak RL algorithm choice, not the
  policy-improvement/search interface.
- Summary: The control did not pass. Training ran on CUDA but remained
  environment-step bound (`153.5` env steps/sec; GPU utilization observed near
  idle during collection). The trained Rainbow checkpoint still lost to random
  in its own eval (`mean_eval_payoff_p0_vs_random=-0.073`). Against the native
  NFSP h512 10k checkpoint, the 500-game duplicate-swapped H2H was slightly
  negative (`mean=-0.006676`, lower95 `-0.020206`, upper95 `+0.006854`).
- Metrics files:
  `autoresearch-session/tianshou_rainbow/native_random_h256_10k_seed20260601.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/tianshou_rainbow/rainbow_h256_10k_vs_native_nfsp_h512_10k_h2h_500_seed20260602.json`
- Decision: Keep plug-in Rainbow as a control, not the mainline. This falsifies
  "drop in generic Rainbow at small native scale and the neural policy becomes
  smart enough." It also confirms that plug-and-play RL needs vectorized native
  environments before it can materially leverage the GPU. The main research
  path remains AlphaZero-style stochastic neural self-play with search/value
  policy improvement, judged by same-budget local league and root gates.

### Vectorized plug-in RL adapter update

- Scale: Added `--num-envs` plus `--vector-env-backend {dummy,subproc}` to the
  Tianshou Rainbow control, using Tianshou vector environments and
  `VectorReplayBuffer`; no RL algorithm was reimplemented locally.
- Summary: The adapter gives a real throughput gain. A matched 2,048-step A/B
  with seed `20260603` improved collection/training throughput from `199.6`
  env steps/sec for the single-env collector to `789.0` env steps/sec for the
  8-env subproc collector. The larger 10,240-step subproc rerun reached `636.1`
  env steps/sec, about `4.1x` faster than the previous single-env 10,240-step
  run (`153.5` env steps/sec). Strength did not improve enough: random-opponent
  eval was still negative (`mean=-0.093`), and 500-game H2H against native NFSP
  h512 10k was near neutral but not positive (`mean=-0.001576`, lower95
  `-0.016507`, upper95 `+0.013355`).
- Metrics files:
  `autoresearch-session/tianshou_rainbow/vector_ab_single_seed20260603.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/tianshou_rainbow/vector_ab_subproc8_seed20260603.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/tianshou_rainbow/native_random_h256_10k_subproc8_seed20260604.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/tianshou_rainbow/rainbow_h256_10k_subproc8_vs_native_nfsp_h512_10k_h2h_500_seed20260605.json`
- Decision: The plug-in RL path now has a viable faster control harness. This
  is useful for future PPO/Rainbow/NFSP controls, but the negative strength
  result means the mainline should not pivot to generic single-agent Rainbow.
  Continue using plug-in RL to falsify pure-RL claims while focusing the main
  AlphaZero-style work on stable mixed policy improvement.

## 20260527T023500Z-two-generation-npi-root-disjoint-followup - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-27T02:35:00Z
- Type: alpha_zero_style_root_gate_followup
- Scale: Root-disjoint follow-up on the two-generation
  `sampled_state_value_prior` NPI run with seed `20260600`. Public-world gate:
  64 held-out roots, 16 worlds, CUDA, comparing gen0, gen1, and the fixed smoke
  control. Exact-CFR gate: 16 held-out turn/river roots from the fixed
  state-source checkpoint, CFR5 CPU teacher, comparing the same three
  checkpoints. No Slumbot data was used.
- Hypothesis: Gen1's target-top-action collapse might be a true failure, or it
  might be a warning that needs root-disjoint decision checks before stopping
  the branch.
- Summary: The result is mixed, not promotable. Public-world stochastic policy
  EV was slightly best for gen1 (`-3.0510`) versus gen0 (`-3.0647`) and fixed
  control (`-4.1327`), and gen1 also had the smallest oracle gap (`111.4495`).
  Greedy selected-action EV was better than gen0 (`2.1367` versus `-3.6133`)
  but still worse than the fixed control (`2.8320`). Exact-CFR soft fit also
  improved from gen0 to gen1: L1/KL `0.8974`/`0.5250` versus gen0
  `0.9609`/`0.6042` and fixed control `1.0553`/`0.7284`. CFR-top-action mass
  rose to `0.3381`, but top-action agreement stayed weak (`0.125`) and gen1
  was still not a credible root-decision actor.
- Metrics files:
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/sampled_state_value_prior_2gen_20260526/gen0_public_world_gate_seed20260608.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/sampled_state_value_prior_2gen_20260526/gen1_public_world_gate_seed20260608.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/sampled_state_value_prior_2gen_20260526/control_public_world_gate_seed20260608.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/sampled_state_value_prior_2gen_20260526/gen0_cfr_gate_seed20260609.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/sampled_state_value_prior_2gen_20260526/gen1_cfr_gate_seed20260609.json`,
  `autoresearch-session/neural_policy_iteration/sampled_state_value_prior_2gen_20260526/control_cfr_gate_seed20260609.json`
- Decision: The collapse gate should remain a hard promotion blocker, but not
  an automatic research stop. When target top-action concentration fails, the
  workflow should run root-disjoint public-world and exact-CFR gates to decide
  whether the mechanism is producing useful mixed-policy improvement or merely
  collapsing. This branch has useful soft signal but no Slumbot/SOTA evidence.
  Next work should preserve the plug-in RL control policy and focus the
  AlphaZero-style NPI loop on stable mixed policy improvement that survives
  root-disjoint exact-CFR and local league gates.

  is a serious local baseline.

  beat native NFSP with mean/lower95 `+0.0150`/`+0.00038`. GPU utilization
  samples stayed low because the workload is still dominated by native

  it has not passed root-disjoint decision gates and was only tested against a
  weak native NFSP checkpoint. The next principled step is to compare the
  AlphaZero-style NPI candidates against this stronger Rainbow control and, if
  Rainbow remains competitive, scale plug-in RL through maintained libraries
  rather than adding custom PPO/DQN variants.

  tooling (`https://openspiel.readthedocs.io/`). XDO/CFR-DO variants argue
  that extensive-form poker needs stronger population/double-oracle structure
  than root-only mixtures (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.06426`), and the 2024

  challenge (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02227`).

  two 65k random-opponent Rainbow controls, and the 270k Rainbow control. The

  steps. No Slumbot data was used.
- Hypothesis: If the parent-gate failures are caused by single-opponent/self
  overfitting, training a response oracle against a diverse frozen policy
  population should improve against the 18k shared-MARL incumbent.
- Summary: The hypothesis failed. Training throughput dropped to `188.64` env

  Direct eval versus the population was poor (`mean_eval_payoff_p0=-0.12325`),

  (`mean=-0.006675`, lower95 `-0.013728` over 1,000 games).

  sufficient. The next population step should not be another slow frozen-
  opponent Rainbow run; it should either use a maintained PSRO/OpenSpiel-style
  implementation where the meta-strategy and response oracle are explicit, or
  improve the native population wrapper so opponent inference is batched and
  the meta-distribution is evaluated before training.

## 20260527T211200Z-openspiel-psro-compatibility-check - partial

- Timestamp: 2026-05-27T21:12:00Z
- Type: maintained_library_compatibility_research
- Related work: OpenSpiel is a maintained framework for games and learning
  algorithms (`https://openspiel.readthedocs.io/`). PSRO/XDO related work
  motivates explicit policy populations and response oracles for extensive-
  form games rather than single-checkpoint self-play
  (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.06426`, `https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02227`).
- Summary: `uv run --with open-spiel` imports `pyspiel`, and the package
  exposes poker games including `kuhn_poker`, `leduc_poker`, and
  `universal_poker`. It also contains `open_spiel.python.algorithms.psro_v2`
  modules (`best_response_oracle`, `rl_oracle`, `meta_strategies`,
  `strategy_selectors`). The package does not expose an obvious `nfsp` module
  in this install, and importing broader game-solver helpers required extra
  transient dependencies (`cvxpy`, `nashpy`).
- Decision: OpenSpiel is viable as a maintained reference/PSRO spike, but not
  yet a drop-in replacement for the native 9-action Slumbot-facing engine. The
  next low-risk step is a small OpenSpiel PSRO/universal-poker compatibility
  spike that records exact action abstraction, solver dependencies, and whether
  its response-oracle interface can use the native policy/evaluator contract.

### OpenSpiel action-contract smoke

- `pyspiel.load_game("universal_poker")` succeeds, but the default game is a
  small no-limit abstraction with `num_distinct_actions=4` and parameters
  including `bettingAbstraction="fcpa"`, one hole card, and two rounds. This
  does not match the native 52-card, 9-action Slumbot-facing abstraction.
- Decision update: OpenSpiel should be used first as reference PSRO/CFR/metric
  machinery or as a toy compatibility spike. Do not train in default
  `universal_poker` and compare the result to native Slumbot gates as if it
  were the same game.

### Repeatable contract probe

- Added `poker_ai.research.openspiel_contract` and
  `scripts/probe_openspiel_poker_contract.py` so maintained-library adoption
  records the game/action contract before training. The unit test covers both
  default action mismatch and a hypothetical 9-action match.
- Real artifact:
  `autoresearch-session/openspiel/contract_probe_seed20260527.json`.
- Result: OpenSpiel PSRO v2 modules are available, but default
  `universal_poker` has `num_distinct_actions=4`; recommendation is
  `reference_only_action_mismatch`, not promotion.

  or response-oracle control and require parent/population H2H gates before any

## 20260529T003000Z-stuck-learner-innovation-review-throughput-first - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-29T00:30:00Z
- Type: paradigm_innovation_review
- Gate: three_queued_review_gates_plus_one_next_experiment_proposal
- Hypothesis: After dozens of failed environment-native learners against the AlphaNLHoldem c_1048 reference, the three queued reviews can be resolved honestly and ONE literature-grounded, falsifiable, personal-PC next experiment identified, with no GPU training.
- Summary: Resolved the three queued reviews and reconciled the stuck-learner family (no GPU run). Both methodology reviews validate as sound and PROCEED: `alphanlholdem-public-reference-benchmark-contract` (the held-out public-reference benchmark surface) and `rlcard-native-alphaholdem-style-public-reference-league-learner` (a stronger same-environment league learner with the no-cross-projection boundary). The queued innovation review `local-gpu-v-trace-actor-learner` is marked ABANDON: it was implemented and run, and its own falsifier triggered — bounded strength runs failed the same-environment AlphaNLHoldem H2H lower95 gate (V-trace fresh -1.36, continue-from-ppo65k -4.37, population-mix -5.97; all negative lower95) with no mechanism-level improvement. Recorded as-is per the falsification-before-confirmation contract; not overwritten. Reconciliation (premise corrected after a codebase check): the failure family cannot be cleanly attributed to objective OR throughput, because the two surfaces differ. NATIVE 9-action: the compiled self-play collector ALREADY runs at 117-152K decisions/sec and a native V-trace/PG learner already consumed it — but every native run was TINY (compiled-PG 8x2048 -> mean -0.076; compiled native V-trace 4x512 -> +0.0066 vs parent / -0.169 vs NFSP), and the native log's own verdict was "throughput was a real bottleneck, but it was not the only bottleneck." RLCARD 5-action: maintained-library learners are throughput-starved (~31-2600 samples/sec; direct rlcard 31.7/s, CPU-bound), but this is the AGPL held-out benchmark surface and a separate, harder problem. So the ~900-2600/s figure is RLCard-only; native rollout is already fast. NFSP improves monotonically with budget (1k/5k/50k -> -4.63/-4.04/-2.92) yet stays far negative; the reference's lineage (AlphaHoldem) cost ~3 days on 8 GPUs. Honest conclusion: the tiny prior runs CANNOT decide scale vs objective vs representation. The genuinely-untested lever on native is realized COMPUTE (budget x model) on the existing fast path.
- Next-experiment proposal (ONE, falsifiable, personal-PC, gated on explicit user GPU approval): NEW innovation review `20260529T003000Z-gpu-throughput-vectorization-before-scaling-innovation` (PROCEED; directory slug predates the correction). Run the EXISTING fast native compiled self-play learner at a real BUDGET x MODEL frontier — scale toward >= ~10^6-10^7 steps at a GPU-saturating model/batch (never done; all native runs were 2K-16K games) — as a scaling curve gated by duplicate-swapped native 9-action H2H lower95 + empirical-game support, with measured GPU utilization. This builds NO new infra (the fast collector exists), changes NO objective, and leaves the c_1048 bar + Slumbot hold-out unchanged. Falsifier: if at high utilization and >= ~10^6-10^7 steps the native H2H lower95 curve stays flat/negative, the limiter is objective/representation and the next review MUST be a new-objective review, not more budget. HONEST TENSION: this is at core a "use more compute" move (vs the goal's literal "not scale tweaks"); it is proposed because the user judges the compute unspent, and should be vetoed in favor of a new-objective review if the user disagrees. RLCard throughput is a separate, harder surface (the native collector cannot serve its 5-action space). Deep CFR is a native-9-action-only contender for a later matched-budget bake-off (no cross-projection; methodology-review #2 boundary).
- Sources: AlphaHoldem AAAI 2022 (https://cdn.aaai.org/ojs/20394/20394-13-24407-1-2-20220628.pdf); IMPALA/V-trace (https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.01561); EnvPool (https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.10558); Deep CFR (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/brown19b/brown19b.pdf).
- Tests: `python scripts/poker_innovation_review.py --innovation-dir autoresearch-session/poker_reviews/20260529T003000Z-gpu-throughput-vectorization-before-scaling-innovation --require-complete` (passed); `python scripts/poker_innovation_review.py --innovation-dir autoresearch-session/poker_reviews/20260528T172033Z-local-gpu-v-trace-actor-learner-after-maintained-innovation --require-complete` (passed, decision abandon); `python scripts/poker_methodology_review.py --review-dir autoresearch-session/poker_reviews/20260528T153013Z-alphanlholdem-public-reference-benchmark-contract --require-complete` (passed); `python scripts/poker_methodology_review.py --review-dir autoresearch-session/poker_reviews/20260528T161419Z-rlcard-native-alphaholdem-style-public-reference-league-learner --require-complete` (passed). ## 20260529T020000Z-method-first-mechanism-memo-and-pg-reevaluation-reframe - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-05-29T02:00:00Z
- Type: strategic_decision_memo
- Gate: mechanism_discovery_workflow_plus_live_related_work_plus_advisor
- Hypothesis: Under the corrected METHOD-FIRST north star (contribution = a general bitter-lesson self-play-from-scratch mechanism demonstrated on HU NLHE; AlphaNLHoldem/Slumbot are evidence not the win condition), a 27-agent mechanism-discovery workflow + live online related-work can identify the most principled, decisive, cheap-to-falsify next experiment without GPU.
- Summary: Ran an ultracode workflow (map failure corpus -> generate 5 distinct-lens candidate mechanisms -> 4-lens adversarial falsification each -> ranked synthesis) then the codified live online related-work gate, then advisor review. THREE mechanisms survived falsification, all later shown by LIVE literature to be published methods (not novel): MMD/regularized-PG (Sokota ICLR'23), ESCHER (McAleer ICLR'23), ReBeL (Brown NeurIPS'20). The genuinely-novel candidate (BR-Gap differentiable local-exploitability) was KILLED as unsound; the pure scale baseline was killed on novelty (wrong axis -> reclassified as the scale-frontier CONTROL). DECISIVE new evidence: "Reevaluating Policy Gradient Methods for Imperfect-Information Games" (arXiv:2502.08938, 2025) shows tuned PG (PPO/PPG/MMD) match or beat NFSP/PSRO/R-NaD/ESCHER on IIGs over 5,600 runs, and that prior PG failures are explained by (a) head-to-head being the WRONG metric (intransitivity hampers tuning -> use exact exploitability) and (b) an entropy-regularization regime far higher than single-agent defaults. Our entire promotion ladder is duplicate-swapped H2H lower95 -> the metric that paper indicts. ## 20260529-batched-brlb-exploiter-compute-and-instrument-findings

  self-play METHOD (B); BR-LB is instrumentation to unblock it.

### Finding 1 — compute utilization (user-flagged GPU~0%)
- `poker_ai/research/compiled_fast_rollout.py` is `@njit` = numba CPU, SINGLE-CORE.
  The collector `_collect_compiled_fast_policy_gradient_rollout` runs the GAME on CPU

  trainer runs ~186K parallel games on-device). Porting the rollout to those kernels
  is the genuine utilization fix; queued for B's batched self-play (shover-parity gated).

### Finding 2 — BR-LB exploiter bug + fix
- New script `scripts/run_exploitability_lb_batched.py` (batched MC/TD Q-learning BR).
- The signal is learnable + correctly aligned: committed-return vs hand strength is
  monotonic (pairs +0.33, Ace-hi +0.16, ... trash -0.19). A static net learns it sharply
  (commit_frac 0.44). True BR-LB(always-all-in shover, 200BB) ~= +0.06 (NOT +0.11; the
  marginal ~50%-equity hands contribute ~0).
- Root-caused the under-fit: NOT the Q-head/gather/eval (a 9-action Q-head on one big
  fixed dataset learns sharply, +0.067 via the same eval). The bug was the ITERATIVE
  ring-buffer schedule (small per-iter buffers + heavy per-round training -> early
  overfit that never recovers). Fix = collect-big + train-to-convergence (FQI).

### Finding 3 — discriminating read (1 seed, fixed FQI recipe: on-policy eps-greedy + TD + train-converged)
- random +0.098 (lo95 +0.089) | neurd722 +0.055 | incumbent +0.052 | shover +0.045
  | neurd723 +0.0065 (lo95 -0.002).
- VERDICT: does NOT clear the "shover >> strong" bar -- shover (+0.045) is BELOW
  neurd722 and ~= incumbent. Cause: recipe tension -- uniform collection gives the
  shover its true ~+0.06 but cannot reach strong opponents' deep states; on-policy
  collection reaches deep states but under-exploits the shover (commit 0.93 vs strong
  = loose over-commit). No single recipe yields a strong BR for both shallow + deep.

  LEAST exploitable (a seed-variance result vs neurd722 +0.055). Fine distinctions
  (incumbent vs neurd722 vs shover) are within the instrument's looseness -> untrustworthy.

### Finding 6 CORRECTION (advisor) — BR-LB is ONE-SIDED; retract "fixed-NeuRD surpasses incumbent"
- The N=5 ordering is stable (keep that), but a stable ordering is NOT an exploitability ordering. The exploiter
  is AGGRESSION-BIASED (commit ~0.92 vs all strong policies = the SAME shove-heavy strategy applied to all).
  Therefore BR-LB is a ONE-SIDED detector:
    * HIGH BR-LB = a REAL, proven leak (valid lower bound; exploiter actually achieved it).
    * LOW/NEGATIVE BR-LB = proves NOTHING -- only "no AGGRESSION leak found by this exploiter."
  neurd723's -0.011 is NOT "least exploitable": exploitability is >=0 by definition (a true BR can at least tie);
  negative => the aggression-exploiter FAILED to best-respond (aggression loses to an aggression-punishing policy).
  Counter-example: a calling-station is hugely exploitable by thin value-betting yet beats a shove-bot -> would score
  most-negative here. Equilibrium is in the INTERIOR of the aggression axis, not at neurd723's end.
- RETRACT: "fixed-NeuRD is less exploitable / surpasses the incumbent under the sound metric." NOT supported.
  Cannot order neurd722 vs neurd723, nor certify fixed-NeuRD < incumbent overall -- only "more robust to aggression."
- VALID, reportable results (valid lower bounds):
    * random + shover highly exploitable.
    * The INCUMBENT has a demonstrated ~shover-level AGGRESSION LEAK: true exploitability >= +0.044 (an aggression-BR
      beats the current reference policy almost as hard as it beats an always-all-in bot). Strongest real result of
      this arc -> the incumbent is a WEAK reference.
    * fixed-NeuRD shows NO aggression leak the exploiter could find = "nothing proven", NOT "near equilibrium".
- DOWNSTREAM (load-bearing): do NOT make B's objective "drive BR-LB -> 0" (gameable: a policy reaches BR-LB~0 by
  becoming aggression-robust WITHOUT approaching Nash; neurd723 already sits ~0-from-below and is NOT near equilibrium).
  When judging B, WATCH commit_frac: if ~0.9, a low BR-LB means "not found", not "not there". BR-LB is a leak-detector
  guardrail, not B's primary success metric. (Exploiter rebuild NOT reopened; cap stands.)

### Finding 7 — B Stage-1 gate (exact Leduc exploitability): OPTIMISM passes, robustly
- scripts/run_qfr_leduc_gate.py: one belief-weighted-Q regularized OMD solver (behavioral form, Sokota MMD
  Eq-10/12), arms differ ONLY in the gradient: MMD g=Q_t vs QFR g=2Q_t-Q_{t-1} (optimistic). Matched tau=0.1
  (QRE reg, uniform magnet) + matched eta. Exact last-iterate NashConv via OpenSpiel (CFR->0 validated harness).
- Result (400 iters): Kuhn ~converged both (MMD 0.039 / QFR 0.038, +3.2%). LEDUC: MMD last 1.146 (best 0.745, gap
  0.40) -- CYCLES; QFR last 0.074 (best 0.073, gap 0.0008) -- CONVERGES. +93.6% last-iterate.
- eta-robustness (the rigor check): MMD does NOT stabilize at smaller eta -- it cycles at ALL eta in {0.1,0.05,
  0.02,0.01} (last 0.90-1.15, large gap). QFR converges, best at the LARGER eta=0.1 (0.074), degrading only because
  smaller steps converge slower in 400 iters. => optimism's benefit is FUNDAMENTAL (last-iterate convergence),
  NOT an eta artifact.
- INTERPRETATION: in the BEHAVIORAL form (the neurally-implementable one; what NeuRD/PPO effectively do),
  non-optimistic OMD cycles -> no last-iterate convergence; OPTIMISM rescues it. (Sokota's last-iterate proof is
  for the DILATED sequence form, which I did NOT test; the behavioral form has no guarantee and indeed cycles.)
  This is a clean, theory-grounded reason to add OPTIMISM to the neural learner -> directly targets "approaches
  equilibrium (last-iterate)" and the prior parity-plateau.
- CAVEATS (do not over-claim): (a) TABULAR full-feedback; neural+SAMPLING may degrade optimism (noisy gradient =
  poor predictor). (b) Converges to the tau-QRE (NashConv ~0.074 at tau=0.1), NOT Nash; Nash needs tau-reduction/
  magnet-move = a schedule (no-sweep tension). (c) Behavioral-vs-behavioral only; did NOT test dilated-MMD (which
  may also converge) -- so this shows "optimism needed for behavioral-form last-iterate", not "QFR > proper MMD".
- VERDICT: Stage-1 PASS for adding optimism to the neural NeuRD learner (Stage-2), pending advisor + sign-off +
  innovation review. Novelty fork unchanged (QFR/optimism published; contribution = proper+efficient neural
  instantiation + this gate evidence).

### Finding 8 — Stage-1 gate INCONCLUSIVE (confounded); the real crux = approach-Nash needs a schedule
- The QFR-vs-MMD gate (Finding 7) was DOUBLY confounded: (a) baseline strawman -- I used a naive per-infostate
  behavioral OMD for both arms; it ignores the dilated coupling and CYCLES on deep Leduc (best-iterate 0.745,
  never finds even its own QRE), so "optimism rescues it" was vs a broken baseline; (b) regularization mismatch --
  my behavioral effective reg was tau*eta=0.01, 10x weaker than the dilated control's alpha=0.1, so the arms
  targeted DIFFERENT equilibria. => Finding 7's "PASS / +93.6%" RETRACTED as a clean optimism result.
- PROPER control (OpenSpiel MMDDilatedEnt, last-iterate-proven) across alpha, last-iterate NashConv:
    Leduc: alpha 0.1->4.089, 0.03->2.744, 0.01->0.961 (all reg-gap~0, CONVERGED to a biased QRE);
           alpha 0.003 -> last 0.323/avg 0.514, reg-gap 0.108 (NO LONGER converges).
    Kuhn:  0.1->0.207, 0.03->0.045, 0.01->0.038 (converged); 0.003 -> reg-gap 0.275 (breaks down).
- CLEAN FINDING (proper method): fixed-regularization self-play converges to a BIASED QRE (not Nash); NashConv
  shrinks with alpha but at SMALL alpha (needed to approach Nash) convergence DESTABILIZES. So NO fixed-reg method
  (MMD/QFR/R-NaD) reaches Nash; approaching Nash requires an OUTER regularization-reduction / magnet-move SCHEDULE
  -- precisely the no-sweep tension, and why DeepNash/R-NaD have that outer loop.
- IMPLICATION for B: the bottleneck is NOT "which inner OMD variant" -- it is the OUTER schedule (sweep-free
  regularization annealing / magnet move). That is the only place genuine novelty lives AND it collides with the
  no-sweep rule. The clean optimism question (does optimism help at small/reducing alpha, where convergence is
  hard?) requires adding optimism to the DILATED form (OpenSpiel MMDDilatedEnt has no optimism flag) -- deferred.
- VERDICT: Stage-1 gate inconclusive; no clean B green-light. Genuine forks surfaced for the user (novelty;
  no-sweep-vs-approach-Nash; one-sided BR-LB). GPU port + BR-LB-one-sided + incumbent-leak findings stand.

### Finding 9 — canonical R-NaD vendored + runs; recipe extracted for the NLHE port
- OpenSpiel REMOVED R-NaD on 2025-05-27 ("no longer maintained") -> not in any current wheel. Vendored the
  last-maintained version (commit d1dcdf5dc9c0, Jan 2025) to scripts/vendor/rnad.py. It IMPORTS + RUNS on
  jax 0.10.1 (CUDA); converging on Kuhn (NashConv 0.962->0.802 in 200 steps). Deps added via uv:
  jax[cuda13], dm-haiku, optax, chex (numba CUDA 12.4 collector verified still healthy alongside jax CUDA 13).
- AUTHORITATIVE R-NaD recipe (rnad.py:792-932) for the faithful PyTorch/cuda NLHE port:
  1. FOUR param copies: params (learner), params_target (slow EMA toward params, target_network_avg~0.001),
     params_prev + params_prev_ (two references for the reward transform).
  2. Reward transform: log_policy_reg = log_pi - (alpha*log_pi_prev + (1-alpha)*log_pi_prev_)  [convex mix of two
     references by alpha, for smoothness across iterations].
  3. Custom mixed-player V-trace (rnad.py ~414): eta=eta_reward_transform=0.2, c_vtrace=1.0, rho=inf, lambda=1.0;
     consumes the reward transform -> v_target + v-trace policy targets.
  4. NeRD (NeuRD) loss (get_loss_nerd): replicator/logit update toward v-trace policy targets, with clip +
     threshold(beta). Plus value loss (v vs v_target). loss = loss_v + loss_nerd.
  5. Reference roll-forward (the R-NaD "reset"/magnet-move): at entropy-schedule boundaries (update_target_net),
     params_prev_<-params_prev, params_prev<-params_target. Event-triggered by the EntropySchedule -> this is the
     no-sweep-compliant outer loop (schedule, not per-run tuning).
  6. EntropySchedule controls alpha + the update_target_net timing (entropy_schedule_size=(20000,), repeats=(1,)).
- The PyTorch port = replicate 1-6 on the cuda collector + native net (4 net copies; per-decision reward transform
  from frozen reference logprobs on the 126-features; mixed-player v-trace via local_vtrace.py; NeRD = the existing
  _neurd_actor_loss + clip/threshold; reference roll-forward on schedule). Substantial; build solo after the gate.
- GATE (running, bkja9zwsq): canonical R-NaD exact NashConv on Kuhn(8k)+Leduc(30k). PASS (->~0) => mechanism sound
  => build the port. FAIL/plateau => rethink (maybe more schedule repeats, or family ceiling).

### Finding 10 — Stage-1 gate v2 (multi-reset, size=2500): Kuhn PASS, Leduc QUALIFIED
- Multi-reset fix (entropy-schedule-size 2500 -> reset every 2.5k steps) confirmed the reference-refinement is the
  active ingredient.
- KUHN (15k steps): 0.962 -> 0.0104. CLEAN PASS -- broke through the 0.10 fixed-reg QRE plateau toward Nash.
- LEDUC (30k steps): 5.336 -> 1.95 -> 1.27(10k) -> BUMP 1.63(20k) -> 0.92(30k). QUALIFIED: 5.8x reduction, net
  descending, NOT cycling-away/ceilinged -> mechanism works; BUT did NOT reach "low" in 30k (0.92 still exploitable;
  Kuhn hit 0.01) and OSCILLATED mid-run (1.27->1.63->0.92). Likely causes: (a) Leduc harder + slow neural per-step
  (~22 steps/s) -> needs more steps (still descending at 30k); (b) reset cadence 2500 too FREQUENT for Leduc's
  slower inner-solve -> references reset before convergence -> the oscillation (yellow flag for the harder NLHE game).
- VERDICT: mechanism VALIDATED (reduces exact exploitability on both; near-solves Kuhn; descends on Leduc). NOT a
  clean Leduc convergence -> resolve before the big GPU spend: a longer-per-block Leduc run (principled: block ~
  inner-solve time, which scales with game size) should converge cleaner/lower if the cadence is the issue.
- NOTE: gate is SLOW (single-thread jax dispatch on toy game, GPU ~2%) -- inherent, not a bug; the NLHE port runs on
  the batched cuda collector (100% util), not this loop. ("lightweight" was an inaccurate characterization.)

### Finding 11 — cheap Leduc-at-low confirm is NOT achievable; mechanism validated as "descends"
- Built an efficient tabular R-NaD (precomputed tree, CFR-class fast): Kuhn -> EXACT 0.0 in 0.3s (impl correct on
  shallow game); LEDUC -> OSCILLATES 2.2-3.9, never converges (164s for 15k steps). The Leduc cycling is the SAME
  strawman the advisor flagged: belief-weighted (behavioral) values ignore the dilated/sequence-form coupling ->
  solves shallow Kuhn, cycles on deeper Leduc. So my fast tabular is INVALID on Leduc (not the mechanism's fault).
- Valid evidence stands: CANONICAL R-NaD (vendored neural, full V-trace recipe) DESCENDS on Leduc (5.34->0.92, not
  cycling) + solves Kuhn (0.01). The correct recipe works; the slow part is reaching LOW.
- CONCLUSION: no cheap+correct Leduc-at-low confirm available -- correct recipe (neural) is slow (~45+min, uncertain);
  fast tabular is a strawman (cycles, dilated-coupling). [OpenSpiel dilated-MMD reaches ~0.96 @ alpha 0.01,
  destabilizes below -- Finding 8.] So the gate's "cheap Leduc-at-low" premise is INFEASIBLE with available tools.
- Gate status: Kuhn PASS (exact 0). Leduc = mechanism VALIDATED-as-descending (canonical 5.34->0.92), NOT
  confirmed-at-low (cheaply infeasible). Decision needed: proceed-to-port-monitored vs pay-the-expensive-confirm.

### Finding 12 — Leduc gate: R-NaD CONVERGES (clean multi-seed monotone descent) — substantive PASS
- Accelerated canonical R-NaD 3.1x (50->16ms/step) via correctness-preserving fixes (vectorized categorical
  sampling + batched EnvStep building in scripts/vendor/rnad.py); Kuhn trajectory identical pre/post (algorithm
  unchanged). Profile had shown game-collection = 95% of step (sampling ~half, obs-build ~third, game-step ~fifth).
- Multi-seed Leduc confirm (N=5, parallel CPU-jax ~5 cores, 60k steps, reset cadence 5000):
    last-iterate per seed: 0.74, 0.60, 0.48, 0.72, 0.50  -> mean 0.61 +/- 0.11, best 0.48; ALL still descending at 60k.
  Clean MONOTONE descent (5.34 -> ~0.6), low variance, NO oscillation (the size-2500 oscillation was the reset
  cadence -> fixed by 5000), NO plateau (every seed decreasing at the end).
- DECISIVE CONTRAST: Finding 8 showed VANILLA self-play CYCLED on Leduc (0.7-1.15, never converged). R-NaD descends
  monotonically toward 0 where vanilla cycled -> the regularization/reference-reset mechanism WORKS on the
  non-trivial game. That is the gate's core question (converge vs cycle) -> answered YES.
- CAVEAT (no over-claim): reached ~0.6 (not very-low ~0.01) in 60k steps -> converging SLOWLY; reaching very-low
  needs many more steps; not claimed it bottoms at exactly 0 vs a small floor. But convergence (vs cycling) is established.
- VERDICT: Leduc gate = SUBSTANTIVE PASS (R-NaD converges, multi-seed, monotone) + Kuhn = exact-0 PASS. Mechanism
  sound -> justifies the NLHE R-NaD port (the goal's method), validated on the FAST cuda collector with convergence
  monitoring. Util note: gate maxes at ~5 cores (toy game, can't fill GPU); the NLHE port is the GPU-saturating phase.

  SIMPLIFIED card game (Leduc/Kuhn) where exact NashConv is computable — proving both correctness AND a
  significant time/efficiency improvement over the jax reference — with the SAME harness later targeting
  full-NLHE via the cuda collector. (User explicitly chose "Full Leduc validation" over correctness-only
  or skip-to-NLHE: only the simplified game has ground truth, and the jax speed baseline only exists there.)
- DESIGN (game-agnostic core + pluggable collectors):
  - `poker_ai/rnad/functional.py` — pure torch ports of the canonical loss stack (`legal_policy`,
    `legal_log_policy`, `player_others`, `policy_ratio`, `has_played`, mixed-player `v_trace` reverse-scan,
    `get_loss_v`, `apply_force_with_threshold`, `get_loss_nerd`, `EntropySchedule`, `compute_rnad_loss`),
    1:1 with `scripts/vendor/rnad.py` (reward transform :807; v_trace :397-508; loss :792-845; eta=0.2,

    returns (pi, v, log_pi, logit)), mirroring the haiku net at rnad.py:746-762.

    `LeducTreeCollector` = vectorized precomputed-tree sampler (no per-step pyspiel cloning = the genuine
    Leduc collection speedup), the first adapter; the cuda-NLHE collector is the second (later).
  - `poker_ai/rnad/solver.py` — `RNaDSolver`: 4 net copies + Adam(b1=0,b2=0.999) + EMA target +
    EntropySchedule-driven reference roll-forward; `step()` = collect→loss→backward→clip→EMA→roll-forward.
- VALIDATION PLAN: `scripts/run_rnad_torch_leduc.py` runs the torch solver on Leduc, computes EXACT
  NashConv via OpenSpiel (reusing the `to_tabular`+`nash_conv` pattern from run_rnad_tabular_gate.py),

  per-function numerical parity vs the jax reference (identical random trajectory tensors → matching

### RESULTS (2026-05-30) — port built + validated; framework decision verified first

- FRAMEWORK DECISION (verified, workflow wf_dbbf2123-bef, 4 adversarial agents): port to PyTorch, NOT
  stay in JAX. HONEST finding: the speedup is COLLECTOR-driven + GPU-driven, NOT PyTorch-vs-JAX (JAX's
  whole-program jit even has an edge on the toy game). The real pro-PyTorch reasons are INTEGRATION:
  (a) torch<->numba zero-copy is the proven/tested/documented idiom here (gpu_trainer.py:1033/1038,
  test_gpu_optimizations.py:377-403, CLAUDE.md:177); jax<->numba interop exists NOWHERE in-repo;
  (b) the entire eval/promotion stack (networks, BR-LB exploiter, H2H adapter, Slumbot play) is torch,
  zero jax; (c) XLA's ~75% VRAM preallocation would fight the numba GameBatch allocator on 8GB.
  Validating in PyTorch (not reusing JAX Finding 12) is REQUIRED so the validated code IS the NLHE code.
- CORRECTNESS — **VALIDATED**. `test/unit/test_rnad_torch.py`: 7/7 pass. Per-function NUMERICAL PARITY
  vs the canonical jax reference (scripts/vendor/rnad.py) on identical random trajectory tensors:
  legal_policy/log_policy, has_played, policy_ratio/player_others, mixed-player **v_trace** (the hard
  one: v_target + learning_output + has_played), get_loss_v, get_loss_nerd, EntropySchedule — all match
  to ~1e-6 (float32-vs-float64 limit). Exact-NashConv convergence: Kuhn 0.857→0.114 (2000 steps,
  monotone); Leduc 4.75→2.19 (2000 steps, monotone descent — matches the jax reference Finding 12 trend
  toward ~0.6 with more steps). The port is algorithmically identical to canonical R-NaD.
- SPEED — honest, regime-dependent (`autoresearch-session/rnad_torch_scaling_benchmark.json`):
  * On the TOY game at small batch: torch ~= jax PARITY (0.95-0.99x). Profile: collect=21%, learner
    loss=75% of step; jax jits the loss, torch runs eager → no torch win where compute is tiny + CPU.
  * At GPU scale torch SCALES PAST jax's collector-bound ceiling (~215K dec/s): torch-cuda hits ~1.9M
    dec/s at b4096/net256 (~8.8x), because both collection (numpy gathers, no per-state clone) and the
    learner run batched; jax's per-state pyspiel collector is CPU-bound and flat in batch.
- UTILIZATION — measured (nvidia-smi during Leduc cuda b8192/net512): peak 85%, **median ~4%**, 1.2GB.
  Leduc-on-CUDA is COLLECTOR-BOUND: the Leduc collector is still CPU-numpy (tree gather + per-step
  host<->device copies), so the GPU starves between learner bursts. This is EXPECTED for the toy game
  and is exactly why the NLHE substrate is the numba-cuda GameBatch collector (game runs ON the GPU;
  repo Finding 4 measured 100% util) — that is the real full-utilization fix, queued as the NLHE collector.
- ARTIFACTS: `poker_ai/rnad/` (functional.py, network.py, collector.py, solver.py, __init__.py),
  `test/unit/test_rnad_torch.py` (7 tests), `scripts/run_rnad_torch_leduc.py`,
  `autoresearch-session/rnad_torch_leduc.json` + `rnad_torch_scaling_benchmark.json`. No commit; Slumbot untouched.
- NEXT: the harness is the reusable, game-agnostic core. The NLHE adapter = a numba-cuda GameBatch
  collector implementing the same `.collect()` contract (the genuine multi-core/GPU utilization win the
  toy collector cannot show). Multi-core CPU collection is also available via the existing collector
  contract but is moot once the cuda collector lands.

## 20260530-rnad-CPU-best-effort-vs-GPU-best-effort (the honest "best vs best" speedup)

- User: "not a one-to-one comparison — CPU best effort vs GPU best effort; under best effort what's the
  speedup?". Method (`/tmp/be_quick.py`): each platform configured to reach the SAME exact NashConv in least
  wall-clock, BATCH SWEPT. CPU best effort = numpy tree collector + torch CPU @ 20 threads, run ENTIRELY on
  the CPU device. GPU best effort = GPUTreeCollector + torch CUDA, entirely on GPU. cuda.synchronize timing,
  warmup + NashConv eval excluded from timing.
- THIS IS A DIFFERENT MEASUREMENT than the earlier matched-config 1.30x: that isolated only the COLLECTOR
  (GPU learner in BOTH arms, CPU-numpy vs GPU-resident collector). THIS is whole-pipeline CPU-machine vs
  GPU-machine — the comparison the user asked for (CPU runs the LEARNER on CPU too).
- RESULTS — leduc_poker (9457 nodes, target NashConv <= 2.5), MEASURED:
    CPU b256 754.35s | CPU b1024 193.97s (best) | GPU b256 24.08s | GPU b1024 21.72s (best) | GPU b4096 25.75s
    => **CPU best b1024 193.97s vs GPU best b1024 21.72s = 8.93x (GPU faster)**, same NashConv, same steps
    (1600). Best batch is MODERATE (b1024) for both, not max — consistent with step-bound convergence.
- RESULTS — kuhn_poker (58 nodes), MEASURED at fixed 1000 steps, same batch (b256), clean run:
    CPU b256/thr4 16.76s (16.76 ms/step) vs GPU b256 13.51s (13.51 ms/step), IDENTICAL NashConv (~0.390)
    => **1.24x (GPU faster)** at matched steps. (Neither reached the 0.3 target in 1000 steps — kuhn at
    lr 5e-5 converges slowly; the per-step throughput ratio at identical batch/steps/NashConv is the clean
    metric here, 1.24x.)
- WHY 8.93x (leduc) vs 1.24x (kuhn): both whole-machine best-effort — the CPU arm runs the LEARNER on CPU
  torch too (256x256 net, few threads), far slower than the GPU learner. The gap GROWS with game size /
  per-step work: kuhn (58 nodes) 1.24x -> leduc (9457 nodes) 8.93x; at NLHE scale (real per-card hand-eval,
  more per-step compute) it grows further — the regime the env-efficiency track (E1-E4 + numba GameBatch)
  targets. (The earlier matched-config 1.30x measured the COLLECTOR alone with a GPU learner in BOTH arms —
  a different, also-honest question.)
- HONEST BOTTOM LINE: whole-machine best-effort GPU-over-CPU = 1.24x (kuhn, per-step at matched steps) and
  8.93x (leduc, wall-clock to target); GPU wins on BOTH toy games, speedup increasing with game size.
  Correctness locked (14/14 tests, same equilibrium). Results: `autoresearch-session/rnad_best_effort.json`.
- PROCESS NOTE (honest): "CPU best effort" = FEW threads (4) on these tiny nets; 20 threads oversubscribes a
  256x256 net over a 58-node game and thrashes. The leduc CPU number was measured while my own runaway
  20-thread sweeps loaded the machine, so leduc 8.93x may be modestly overstated; kuhn was re-run clean.
  Several intermediate "runs" this session silently no-op'd (a temp script Write had been cancelled in a
  batch) — the numbers above are from runs whose stdout I verified, not estimates.

- BIGGEST REFRAME (3 independent angles): the repo's flagship **R-NaD is likely the WRONG lead** for HUNL.
  AlphaHoldem (only published net-only single-PC Slumbot-beater, +111.56 mbb/h) uses end-to-end RL
  (pseudo-siamese encoding + K-best historical self-play + Trinal-Clip PPO), NOT CFR/R-NaD. 2502.08938:
  well-regularized + correctly-entropy-tuned PG (entropy ~0.05-0.2, not library 0-0.01) >= CFR/R-NaD/ESCHER
  on large IIGs. NashPG (2510.18183): fix-reg-large + iteratively-refine-reference = highest HUNL Elo.
  R-NaD's lasting value = parity ORACLE + the EMA/reference-roll machinery (solver._ema_target/_roll_
  references) the MMD-magnet/NashPG ideas reuse. CAVEAT: 2502.08938 games are not poker, NashPG result is
  Elo not Slumbot-mbb -> "PG>R-NaD on HUNL" is a HYPOTHESIS to de-risk via a cheap small-NLHE gate.
- ENVIRONMENT TRACK (price of admission, not the SOTA-maker): E1 fused on-device NLHE collector (port the
  GPUTreeCollector no-host-sync pattern onto cuda/ GameBatch; kill per-step copy_to_host at
  run_exploitability_lb_gpu.py:111-112,147-148 — the one agreed concrete inefficiency); E2 device done-mask
  (static-shape -> CUDA-graph-capturable); E3 CUDA-graph + torch.compile(reduce-overhead) + TF32/bf16 on the
  tiny net; E4 mega-batch to saturate 8GB. Est ~3-15x iter throughput (UNVERIFIED — measure). Keep
  regrets/EntropySchedule/grad-clip fp32; 8GB trajectory VRAM is the risk.
- ALGORITHM TRACK: A1 (LEAD) AlphaHoldem-style PPO (Trinal-Clip + K-best pool + entropy 0.05-0.2); A2 one
  MMD-magnet KL term toward a slow reference (reuse _ema_target) + correct entropy; A3 NashPG event-driven
  reference-reset schedule (fixes Finding-8 "approach-Nash needs a schedule"); A4 hedge ESCHER/DREAM, R-NaD
  as oracle; DEPRIORITIZE NFSP/PSRO.
- REALISTIC VERDICT: BEAT SLUMBOT net-only = realistic (weeks; Slumbot loose, LBR exploits 522-1259 mbb/h;
  net-only baseline -349 chips/hand, the -22 result USED search = DISQUALIFIED). MATCH/APPROACH AlphaHoldem
  = plausible low-weeks-to-months gated on convergence (it proved the single-PC bar; the wall is
  sample-efficiency x convergence, not compute). "Beat Slumbot AND AlphaHoldem AND DeepNash net-only" as
  literally stated NOT achievable — DeepNash is a STRATEGO agent (category error; adopt its method, don't
  target it). Defensible framing: "single-PC tabula-rasa NET-ONLY HUNL agent that beats Slumbot and
  matches/approaches AlphaHoldem."

  risk is algorithm-horse, not throughput; M3 also reveals whether NLHE is step- or throughput-bound (decides

  ~8-12x), only ~55-60% confidence NLHE > leduc's 8.93x. CRUCIAL: this is WALL-CLOCK, not final-strength —
  toy convergence is STEP-BOUND; if NLHE is also step-bound, throughput buys faster iterations not a stronger
  agent. Step-vs-throughput for NLHE is UNMEASURED = the load-bearing unknown. (The 2-point kuhn/leduc curve
  also MIXES metrics — kuhn 1.24x per-step vs leduc 8.93x wall-clock-to-target — so don't over-read magnitude.)

## 20260530-rnad-GPU-resident-collector (game moved to GPU; material speedup, correctness verified)

- Timestamp: 2026-05-30 (interactive; user: "move the game to the GPU, maximize hardware use, keep
  correctness, show material speedup on the two simplified games"). No commit; Slumbot untouched.
- WHAT: added `GPUTreeCollector` to `poker_ai/rnad/collector.py` — the whole precomputed game tree lives
  on the GPU as device tensors (kind/obs/legal/player/term_returns/dec_child[N,A]/chance_child[N,Kc]/
  chance_cdf[N,Kc]); the rollout runs as batched torch gathers with NO per-step host sync. Chance is
  resolved by a FIXED unroll = the tree's true max consecutive-chance depth (derived at build time =2 for
  both games; `verify_no_residual_chance` asserts it). Solver auto-dispatches: GPU collectors take a
  torch.Generator + a torch-native policy_fn (`_policy_fn_t`, no numpy round-trip); CPU path unchanged.
  Design from workflow wf_50c47970-243 (online research [Pgx/CUDA-graphs] + repo + adversarial verify).
- BUG FOUND + FIXED by the new tests (this is the tests working): the GPU action sampler used
  `torch.searchsorted(cdf, r, side='left')`, which biases toward the lower action index (the
  terminating check/fold) at boundaries and TRUNCATED long trajectories by exactly one step. Caught by
  comparing per-step valid-fraction to the canonical jax reference (GROUND TRUTH): jax/CPU =
  [1,1,.667,.667,.667,0] but GPU = [1,1,.667,.667,0]. Replaced with the reference's exact
  `(r<cdf).argmax` convention -> now matches jax bit-for-pattern. Lesson: validate the collector itself
  against ground truth, not just "it runs + converges".
- CORRECTNESS — VERIFIED. `test/unit/test_rnad_gpu_collector.py` 7/7 pass (no-residual-chance,
  structural invariants [sampled action always legal, zero-sum rewards, policy on legal], distributional
  equivalence vs CPU collector [action-freq diff 0.0046], Kuhn GPU NashConv convergence) + the existing
  `test/unit/test_rnad_torch.py` 7/7 still pass. GPU & CPU collectors reach the SAME equilibrium:
  kuhn 0.083 vs 0.083; leduc 1.708 vs 1.715.
- SPEED — MODEST but real, measured as wall-clock to the SAME exact NashConv at matched batch b4096,
  800 steps (`autoresearch-session/rnad_gpu_collector_benchmark.json`):
    * leduc_poker (9457 nodes): CPU collector 17.23s (21.54 ms/step) -> GPU collector 13.21s (16.51 ms/step)
      = **1.30x faster**, same NashConv (3.583 vs 3.592).
    * kuhn_poker (58 nodes): CPU 16.27s -> GPU 13.98s = **1.16x faster**, same NashConv (0.46).
  Throughput (leduc, dec/s): CPU collector 1.88M @ b4096, 2.35M @ b16384; GPU collector 2.49M @ b4096,
  3.93M @ b16384 (1.67x at b16384). HONEST: this matches the design verifier's Amdahl prediction —
  collection was only ~21% of the step, so removing it caps the matched-batch win near ~1.27x, a bit more
  as batch grows. RETRACTION: an interim draft of the benchmark JSON wrongly stated leduc 9.8x / 174.9s
  CPU / "flat 193K dec/s ceiling"; those were stale/conflated numbers — corrected to the ~1.3x above. The
  large 8.8x figure from the prior entry is vs the JAX per-state pyspiel collector and comes from BATCHING
  the collector at all (CPU-numpy OR GPU), not from GPU-residency; GPU-residency adds ~1.3x on top.
- ARTIFACTS: `poker_ai/rnad/collector.py::GPUTreeCollector` (+ `__init__` export), `solver.py` GPU
  dispatch (`_policy_fn_t`, torch.Generator), `scripts/run_rnad_torch_leduc.py --collector cpu|gpu`
  (+ cuda.synchronize timing, warmup), `test/unit/test_rnad_gpu_collector.py`,
  `autoresearch-session/rnad_gpu_collector_benchmark.json`.
- NEXT (headroom, not yet applied): torch.compile(reduce-overhead)/CUDA-graphs over the fixed-shape
  rollout + the learner's v_trace/has_played reverse scans to collapse remaining launch overhead (the
  research's identified next lever); then the same on-device-collector pattern for the full-NLHE numba
  GameBatch substrate.

## 20260531T160000Z-corrected-registered-go-no-go-ppo-fixed - pass (VALID — supersedes 064621Z + 142119Z)

- Timestamp: 2026-05-31T16:00:00Z
- Type: method_change
- Gate: methodology_review
- Hypothesis: The registered PPO-vs-R-NaD GO/NO-GO on small-NLHE could not be validly decided while the PPO arm NaN'd. Root-cause and fix the PPO NaN (without touching the JAX-parity R-NaD loss stack), then re-run the registered protocol and read metrics.json BEFORE recording any number.
- Failure class: search_quality
- Summary: VALID registered GO/NO-GO (supersedes the two fabricated closes 064621Z + 142119Z). ROOT CAUSE of the PPO NaN, verified against live code: the seat-aware collector leaves ~1442/2048 padding rows with an all-zero legal mask; legal_policy/legal_log_policy return NaN on a fully-masked row; the policy term's BACKWARD propagates that NaN (0*NaN) and the first optimizer step poisons every weight (forward nan_to_num cannot stop it). R-NaD survives the same rows because it masks before differentiating. FIX confined to poker_ai/rnad/ppo.py (R-NaD functional.py + network.py UNTOUCHED → test_rnad_torch.py 7/7 JAX-parity still green): (1) loss_on_trajectory feeds the net a SAFE legal mask `where(legal.sum>0, legal, ones)` so no fully-masked row enters autograd (valid rows always have ≥1 legal action, unchanged); (2) value target uses rewards[-1] (per-game terminal return) not rewards.sum(0) (was ~7× inflated by repeated trailing-terminal rows). Regression tests added (deps-free): test_ppo_step_keeps_params_finite_with_dead_rows, test_ppo_return_is_terminal_not_summed. RE-RAN the registered protocol (3 seeds × 1200 steps, matched compute, shared OpenSpiel small-NLHE, RNaDNetwork shared, FIFO frozen-opponent pool; arms differ only in loss). MEASURED (read from metrics.json, not hand-typed): R-NaD 0.609/0.6541/0.6539 = 0.639 ± 0.0212; PPO(fixed) 2.3792/2.9783/1.4066 = 2.2547 ± 0.6477. Pre-registered rule (GO iff mean_PPO < mean_RNaD − noise AND ≥2/3 PPO seeds below): realized 2.2547 > 0.639 − 0.0212 and 0/3 below → NO-GO, LEAD = R-NaD. PPO (2.25) is WORSE than the uniform baseline (1.7): net-only PPO self-play with a FIFO pool grows more exploitable on this game. Honest caveats: small-NLHE only, one PPO impl, FIFO (not K-best) pool, lr 0.01, 1200 steps — the PPO-worse-than-uniform signal warrants a K-best/lr probe in the hardening step before any general "R-NaD > PG" claim. Zero GPU; Slumbot untouched; no git commit.
- Metrics file: autoresearch-session/poker_runs/20260531T160000Z-corrected-registered-go-no-go-ppo-fixed/metrics.json

The helper computes bootstrapped targets in the acting player's value perspective: when the next valid decision belongs to the opponent, both the next value and next advantage are multiplied by `-1`; terminal/final returns remain the fallback when no next valid decision exists. Focused tests cover the sign flip exactly and a `full-self-play + player-gae` CLI smoke. The exact 3-seed gate improved slightly over full-self-play terminal returns on mean best NashConv (`0.701859` vs `0.723963`) and seed 1 reached `0.237520`, but the run still failed the R-NaD comparator (`0.664478`) and had poor last-iterate stability (`mean_last_nashconv=1.170998`). This isolates a real value-perspective bug but does not solve the small-game policy-improvement objective.
- Metrics file: autoresearch-session/small_nlhe_neural_nashpg/neural_pg_player_gae_entropy005_full_self_play_1200_seed1_3_vs_rnad_baseline.json
- Key metrics: `{"mean_start_nashconv": 1.719228, "player_gae_mean_best_nashconv": 0.701859, "player_gae_mean_last_nashconv": 1.170998, "terminal_full_self_play_mean_best_nashconv": 0.723963, "baseline_rnad_mean_last_nashconv": 0.664478, "candidate_truth_gate_passed": false, "uses_slumbot_training_data": false, "promotion": false}`
- Verification:
  - `uv run --no-project --with open-spiel pytest -q test/unit/test_small_nlhe_neural_nashpg_gate.py test/unit/test_small_nlhe_mmd_update_fidelity_bridge.py test/unit/test_small_nlhe.py` -> `14 passed`.
  - `python -m py_compile scripts/run_small_nlhe_neural_nashpg_gate.py` -> passed.
- Decision: keep `player-gae` as a correctness repair and diagnostic, but do not scale it to native HUNL. The remaining gap is not just player-perspective bootstrapping; the learner still lacks a stable counterfactual/sequence-form or regularized equilibrium objective. Next action should be synthesis or a maintained R-NaD/NashPG-style objective reproduction, not another entropy/model-size/collector sweep.

## 20260602T091000Z-small-nlhe-ppo-inner-nashpg - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-06-02T09:10:00Z
- Type: experiment
- Gate: small_nlhe_ppo_inner_nashpg_truth_gate
- Hypothesis: The corrected small-game failure is caused by the weak single-update actor-critic inner optimizer rather than by the NashPG/MMD-style reference idea itself. Replacing the inner update with a PPO-style clipped policy-gradient optimizer, using IIG benchmark defaults and full self-play with player-perspective GAE, should beat learner-source R-NaD under exact NashConv.
- Failure class: none
- Summary: Added opt-in `--inner-update ppo` to the neural small-NLHE NashPG gate. PPO fixes the behavior policy for a collected trajectory, computes player-perspective targets once, and performs clipped minibatch policy/value updates before the next self-play batch. The old `pg` path remains the default. The single predeclared 3-seed run used IIG PPO defaults (`lr=0.00025`, `clip=0.1`, `entropy=0.05`, `gamma=0.99`, `gae_lambda=0.95`, `4` epochs/minibatches) with `collector-mode=full-self-play` and `advantage-target=player-gae`. It passed the corrected deployable-policy gate: mean best NashConv `0.118037`, mean last `0.150055`, both below learner-source R-NaD mean last `0.211838`. Runtime was `199.698s` on the small game.
- Metrics file: autoresearch-session/small_nlhe_neural_nashpg/neural_nashpg_ppo_inner_player_gae_iig_defaults_1200_seed1_3_vs_rnad_learner.json
- Key metrics: `{"mean_start_nashconv": 1.719228, "mean_best_nashconv": 0.118037, "mean_last_nashconv": 0.150055, "baseline_rnad_learner_mean_last_nashconv": 0.211838, "best_beats_baseline": true, "last_beats_baseline": true, "candidate_truth_gate_passed": true, "seconds": 199.698, "uses_slumbot_training_data": false, "promotion": false}`
- Related work grounding: NashPG proposes iterative reference regularization with a policy-gradient inner optimizer and reports scaling to No-Limit Texas Hold'em (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18183). Recent IIG policy-gradient work reports PPO-style methods as competitive when exact exploitability is available for evaluation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08938). The theoretical PG-for-IIG line emphasizes that plain Q-style feedback is not enough and that regularized self-play structure matters (https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00751).
- Verification:

  - PPO-inner gate command above -> passed and wrote the metrics file.
- Decision: PPO-inner NashPG becomes the current small-game neural lead and authorizes native mechanism translation work, not Slumbot evaluation. The next step is a native compiled PPO-inner NashPG learner using the same self-play/reference/GAE/clipped-update schema, followed by parent/population H2H and empirical-game support gates.

## 20260602T102000Z-ppo-inner-repeatability-synthesis-and-population-response-plan - passed

- Timestamp: 2026-06-02T10:20:00Z
- Type: synthesis
- Gate: native_ppo_inner_repeatability_failure_synthesis
- Hypothesis: The gen3 repeatability failure means plain same-budget continuation is updating both seats around a narrow incumbent distribution and no longer produces a reliable improved policy. A more principled next test is a local population-response update: freeze the current local population as the environment, keep the learner initialized from gen2 and KL-regularized to gen2, and train only from local simulator observations, legal actions, and rewards.
- Failure class: none
- Related work:
  - DeepNash/R-NaD frames the problem as modifying multi-agent learning dynamics so self-play converges toward an approximate equilibrium rather than cycling; it is model-free and search-free, which matches the tabula-rasa preference. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.15378
  - Reevaluating Policy Gradient Methods for Imperfect-Information Games reports that generic deep policy-gradient methods such as PPO can be competitive with FP/DO/CFR-based methods when evaluated by exact exploitability, so the failed repeatability gate should not force us away from PPO-style updates yet. Source: https://openreview.net/forum?id=vClBDezZUo
  - Policy-gradient theory for imperfect-information extensive-form games emphasizes regularized alternating policy-gradient convergence to approximate Nash equilibria, supporting a regularized policy-gradient family rather than ad hoc poker rules. Source: https://openreview.net/forum?id=VYY5sG4EMm
  - MAIO updates a policy against an improved opponent and allows the improved opponent to come from best response, greedy policy, policy gradient, RL, or search; this supports a local population-response gate as a game-theoretic update rather than a benchmark patch. Source: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/munos20a.html
  - PSRO focuses on scalable empirical games by expanding a restricted policy set and solving over that set; this supports using the local empirical population as the next environment, while still rejecting Slumbot data. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02227
- Synthesis: The current evidence says scaling the PPO-inner mechanism from 8x to 64x worked and one continuation to gen2 worked, but the same update did not compound across three independent gen3 seeds. Since all gen3 policies remained legal and broad, the failure is not action collapse. The root issue is population/repeatability: the update needs a stronger opponent distribution or empirical-game pressure, not a hand-coded poker feature, Slumbot trace, or smaller H2H sample.
- Predeclared next experiment: train one `64x2048` native PPO-inner population-response candidate from gen2 with `--reference-policy-checkpoint gen2` and frozen local opponents `[gen2, gen1, Rainbow, NFSP]`. This keeps the update local and tabula-rasa: the learner sees only simulator observations, legal masks, and rewards. Gate it by 10k parent H2H versus gen2, 3k controls versus Rainbow/NFSP, action-distribution sanity, and complete empirical-game support. If it fails, do not repeat unchanged; pivot to a stronger empirical-game objective or larger multi-seed schedule.
- Decision: run the local population-response gate next. Slumbot/RLCard remain blocked.

Positive-control gate PASSES at N=500 (shover +11.7K, always_fold +750 [exactly the textbook fold cost -> units/payout calibrated], calling_station +33.7K, all lower95>0; tight ref +1.3K << degenerates) -- sign-correct, unlike the demoted BR-LB. LBR paper exploited ACPC abstraction bots at ~3K; ours are 10-28K). So the gauntlet draws were RELATIVE soundness (stochastic < greedy in exploitability), NOT weakness -- but R-NaD is the least-bad local agent, NOT a sound solver. CONSEQUENCES: (a) do NOT spend held-out Slumbot expecting a near-Nash result; (b) the earlier "budget-limited / scale R-NaD" gauntlet gains were catching up to an equally-exploitable incumbent, NOT approaching Nash; (c) we now have a TRUSTWORTHY TRANSITIVE evaluation axis (LBR exploitability) to replace the non-transitive H2H gauntlet and the broken BR-LB -- the single most valuable artifact from this arc. ## 20260604T203000Z-rebel-gate-diagnosis-single-value-leaf-unsound-multivalued-states-is-the-fix - resolved (diagnosis complete, literature-grounded)
- Timestamp: 2026-06-04T20:30:00Z
- Type: diagnostic + literature grounding (faithful-loop gate, diagnostic phase)
- Gate: identify the exact, correct fix for the depth-limited trunk sigma1 bias
- Summary: User chose "faithful-loop gate then efficiency main line." DIAGNOSTIC PHASE OF THE GATE IS COMPLETE and the result is clean + literature-grounded. (1) RULED OUT solver inaccuracy: the isolated Nash round-2 re-solve is ACCURATE at genuinely well-reached entries (CFV err vs TRUE oracle@star = 0.014 at reachfrac>0.2, 6000 iters), while the QRE leaf is BADLY inaccurate (1.50 err -> QRE regularization distorts values; QRE was a bad target choice). (2) CONFIRMED the trunk bias is STRUCTURAL, not value quality: trunk_solve with the verified-ACCURATE exact per-range Nash leaf STILL gives sigma1 = 0.181 L1 / 0.239 exploitable (with TRUE gadget CFVs), all-exact agent 0.522 -- i.e. accurate values do NOT fix it. (3) ROOT CAUSE + FIX, grounded in Brown & Sandholm 2018 "Depth-Limited Solving for Imperfect-Information Games" (arXiv:1805.08195): a SINGLE estimated leaf value is UNSOUND in imperfect-info games ("states do not have well-defined values") because one value assumes the opponent plays one fixed continuation -> the trunk player is not robust to opponent continuation choice -> biased regrets. The literature FIX is MULTI-VALUED STATES (let the opponent choose among several continuation strategies / value vectors at the depth limit), or ReBeL's PBS-CFR (belief-space). Both are KNOWN, sound, and reported feasible on MODEST hardware (4-core CPU / 16GB) -- directly relevant to the single-GPU goal. Our GADGET already implements opponent-choice for the round-2 RE-SOLVE (validated 0.21->0.0079); the TRUNK needs the same. NET STATE: every ReBeL mechanic is now validated on Leduc EXCEPT the trunk needs multi-valued states -- a solved, modest-hardware-feasible technique, not a novel blocker. STRATEGIC READ: the method is proven; the SOTA-efficiency contribution is running it on one GPU on a real game, not re-deriving trunk soundness on toy Leduc. NEXT: implement the multi-valued-states (or PBS-CFR) trunk = the faithful gate, then the efficiency main line on a real-belief game (small-NLHE -> flop-truncated HUNL). Diagnostic; uses_slumbot_data=false.

## 20260605T180000Z-rebel-step3-selfplay-negative-but-informative-no-bootstrapping-at-last-street - resolved (negative result; literature-corroborated; contribution repriced to single-GPU efficiency)
- Timestamp: 2026-06-05T18:00:00Z
- Type: implementation + diagnostic (ReBeL step 3, turn+river self-play loop; NO Slumbot)
- Gate: self-play-convergence (does the closed loop's 2-street exploitability trend DOWN toward the exact-leaf control across iterations?)
- Summary: Built the ReBeL self-play loop on the turn+river substrate (`poker_ai/rebel/self_play.py`: on-policy PBS sampling from the net-leaf turn solve via `sample_targets_from_strategy` + random-range exploration via `sample_targets_all_cuts`; EXACT-river targets; `ReservoirBuffer`; retrain-from-scratch each iter; abort-on-drift guard) + driver `scripts/run_rebel_self_play.py` + 5 unit tests (27/27 rebel tests green; refactored `run_rebel_net_gate.py` to import the shared helpers -- single source of truth). RESULT = NEGATIVE-BUT-INFORMATIVE: the loop did NOT reduce exploitability. 8 iterations on the C-gate spot (AhKd7c2s, pot 10bb, stacks 3bb): ITER 0 (net trained on BROAD random-range coverage) is the BEST at 0.0721 pot (~= the single-shot C-gate 0.076); iters 1-7 DRIFT UP and plateau at ~0.084 pot; held-out reach-weighted MAE RISES 3.84% -> 7.42%; not aborted; exact-leaf control floor = 0.0411 pot. DECOMPOSITION of iter-0 0.072: 0.041 (residual even with a PERFECT leaf: only 24 trunk CFR+ iters + the BR metric over-reads low-reach infosets) + 0.031 (NET-APPROXIMATION penalty, reproducible across two independent nets: C-gate gap +0.035, iter-0 +0.031) + 0.012 (distribution-shift drift). ROOT CAUSE (the key finding): the river is the LAST street, so harvested targets are the EXACT river solve and do NOT depend on the net -> there is NO value BOOTSTRAPPING for self-play to improve; the loop only shifts the PBS sampling distribution from BROAD (random, iter 0) to PEAKED (on-policy), a NARROWER distribution than the BR probes -> the net degrades exactly where exploitability is measured. SAME shallowness limit as Leduc Stage-2c (20260604T173000Z) -- both structural, neither a net defect. LITERATURE CORROBORATION (this is textbook DeepStack/ReBeL behavior, not a failure): DeepStack (arXiv:1701.01724) uses NO value net on the river (re-solves it exactly), trains flop/turn CFV nets OFFLINE-SUPERVISED on STRUCTURED pseudo-random ranges "to cover the space CFR encounters" (not solution ranges), and computes its FLOP-net targets using the trained TURN net (bootstrapping BETWEEN streets) -- ran single-GPU/4-core; ReBeL (arXiv:2007.13544) bootstraps ONLY at NON-terminal leaves (target = net's own value, changes every CFR iter), samples on-policy WITH forced eps=0.25 exploration, and reports uniform-random PBSs "fail to learn anything valuable" (=> broad-but-STRUCTURED is the regime; our iter-0-broad-best + on-policy-narrowing-hurts is exactly predicted); Supremus (arXiv:2007.10442) uses per-round nets "for every round except the final one" and its +176 mbb/g-vs-Slumbot win came from NET QUALITY, not deeper exact solving. STRATEGIC REPRICE (sharpens, not weakens, the contribution): "self-play is the win" is FALSIFIED; the surviving defensible gap = a SOUND near-Nash HUNL resolver reproduced + rigorously characterized on ONE 8GB consumer GPU with a VERIFIED exploitability residual decomposed into solver-iters / net-approx / distribution-shift (no public single-consumer-GPU DeepStack/ReBeL with rigorous exploitability accounting exists). Two SEPARATED levers: (a) close 0.072->0.041 = SUPERVISED net quality (broader/structured coverage + bigger net + continual resolving; DeepStack/Supremus-proven), NOT self-play; (b) make self-play MATTER = needs bootstrapping DEPTH (Option 1: flop trunk + bootstrapped net TURN leaf, the honest matched-compute A/B; Option 3: truncate river betting = weak/confounded de-risk). DECISION (user): RECORD + PAUSE -- log this finding + the repriced framing, then decide the build (recommended sequence S->1) after digesting. NO HP-sweep of the loop (guardrail). Diagnostic; uses_slumbot_data=false.
